articles.title: Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
articles.summary:
Apple released betas of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and macOS 27.3 today, and the company is using the update to test new per device daily usage limits for some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features, according to MacRumors.
Apple is testing daily usage limits for more complex Siri AI interactions
Frequent users of some Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features will require an iCloud Plus subscription to avoid limits.
Basic Siri commands and requests will remain free and unlimited, but more advanced features that rely on cloud-based processing like generating, cleaning up, or extending images in Photos will be subjected to the daily limits. There are four categories of limited usage, MacRumors reports, including using Siri AI for “multi-step, personal context requests,” image generation and editing tools, automations in Shortcuts that “rely on Apple Foundation Cloud and Cloud Pro Models,” and third-party apps that use those same cloud models.
Apple hasn’t specified exactly how many times those features and tools can be used each day before limits are reached, but they’ll vary based on the task. The company reportedly plans to provide notifications when users are approaching their limit and have finally reached it.

articles.title: NVIDIA Announces Rubin HPC — A New GPU to Accelerate Agents for Science, Engineering and Analytics

Announced today at SC26, NVIDIA Rubin HPC is a new GPU in the NVIDIA Vera Rubin platform designed to accelerate simulation and data processing for science, engineering and analytics workflows.
As agents help scientists and engineers explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs, they rely on simulations to test those ideas and guide their next steps. Rubin HPC will accelerate those simulations, shortening the path from exploration to scientific discovery and industrial design.
The Rubin HPC GPU features a record number of CUDA cores — more than 50,000 on a single GPU — as well as a sparse data acceleration capability that keeps those cores fed with data, and accelerates GPU-to-GPU connectivity with seventh-generation NVIDIA NVLink interconnect technology.
Scientists and engineers rely on simulation to understand complex systems before committing to experiments or physical prototypes. Working with agents, these teams can explore more candidate materials, molecules and designs. This increases demand for the GPU-accelerated simulations needed to evaluate those ideas and guide next steps.
“For agents tackling science and engineering, faster simulation means faster discovery,” said Ian Buck, vice president of hyperscale and high-performance computing at NVIDIA. “Rubin HPC accelerates the simulations agents use to test ideas and guide their next steps, helping scientists and engineers explore more possibilities and bring breakthroughs closer.”

articles.title: Microsoft Rules Out Cyberattack in Outage, Warns of Phishing Campaign
articles.summary:
Microsoft says its recent Microsoft 365 outage was not caused by a cyberattack, but warns that attackers used the disruption to send phishing emails disguised as service notifications.
The November 12 outage disrupted access to Exchange Online mailboxes and Outlook. The tech giant also identified possible effects on services such as Teams, SharePoint Online and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Organizations and government agencies in several countries reported interruptions to email and other operations.
“This was a technical issue not related to cyber or AI / agents,” Microsoft said in a statement on Friday.
The company traced the failure to an earlier network capacity upgrade, with a subsequent network change exposing the problem. Microsoft said it fixed the underlying issue and was bringing services back in stages to ensure they remained stable. The Exchange Online incident, tracked as EX1550543, was marked resolved on November 13.
Microsoft Threat Intelligence said it observed a phishing campaign exploiting the disruption. The fake emails posed as Microsoft 365 service health notices and referred to EX1550543, the actual incident identifier.
In some messages detected on November 13, recipients were falsely told that emails held during the outage would be deleted within 24 hours unless they clicked a link to restore them.

articles.title: VIDÉO : Recalé au contrôle antipollution, il pirate le calculateur de sa Jeep de 1994 avec deux IA et réussit son coup
articles.summary:
Depuis quelques semaines, Muhammad Zulali faisait face à un problème.
Sa Jeep Cherokee de 1994 échouait au contrôle antipollution californien, obligatoire pour renouveler l’immatriculation, et chaque nouveau passage chez le technicien lui coûtait une centaine de dollars.
Plutôt que de continuer à changer des pièces au hasard, celui qui précise ne pas être mécanicien a passé près d’une semaine à faire travailler deux agents de programmation sur le calculateur moteur, d’abord Claude Code d’Anthropic, puis Codex d’OpenAI.
Il a raconté l’expérience dans une vidéo YouTube publiée le 10 novembre, qui a frôlé 1,5 million de vues en moins d’une semaine. Un succès que l’on doit également au résultat de l’expérience : la Jeep a fini par réussir son contrôle.
Une voiture trop ancienne pour les outils de diagnostic actuels
Avant que son propriétaire ne se lance dans cette expérience folle, le problème avait bien été identifié. Au palier de 25 mph (environ 40 km/h), la Jeep rejetait trop d’oxydes d’azote (NOx), des polluants qui se forment quand le moteur reçoit trop d’air par rapport au carburant.
Le propriétaire a d’abord remplacé la sonde lambda, qui mesure l’oxygène dans l’échappement, mais la voiture a alors échoué dès le palier de 15 mph (environ 24 km/h).

articles.title: Did Canada lose its AI chip champions?
articles.summary:
Last month, Toronto-founded AI chip maker Tenstorrent announced a whopping $1.5-billion USD Series E round. I say Toronto-founded because the company quietly relocated to the US in 2023 to support its fundraising and IPO goals. With over $2 billion USD in funding announced since, the move appears to have paid off.
Tenstorrent still has some 200 employees in Toronto, and hasn’t forgotten its Canadian roots. The Logic reported this week that the company has lobbied the federal government for sovereign AI contracts and funding for large-scale data centre buildouts.
Every company should be expected to make decisions in its own best interests. But Tenstorrent’s gentle tap dance back and forth across our southernmost border when it benefits them shines a light on a murky question: what makes a company Canadian?
Noting that the feds’ Buy Canadian Policy currently allows for, say, Walmart Canada, the policy wonks at The Canadian Shield Institute have argued for a revised definition in BetaKit. The think tank also recently asserted the perils of considering companies like Tenstorrent Canadian enough: “If any company, headquartered anywhere on earth, can qualify for funding because its lobbyists point to some operations here or some historic association with Canada, then economic development policy will become meaningless.”

articles.title: Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Use prompt caching with open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock
Many generative AI applications send the same long context with every request, and prompt caching avoids processing it again each time. That context can be a system prompt, reference documents, tool definitions, or the conversation so far. Open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock can reuse it across requests, which helps reduce input costs and response latency.
Prompt caching reuses the computed state of a matching prompt prefix, so repeated context is read from cache instead of being processed again. Amazon Bedrock manages the cache for you. Depending on the model, you can use implicit caching, which works automatically, explicit caching, where you mark the reusable prefix, or both. The more context you reuse, and the more often you reuse it, the more you can save.
As with other models on Amazon Bedrock, your prompts and outputs aren’t shared with the model provider or used to train models. For more information, see Data protection in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide.
Open-weight models on Amazon Bedrock now support explicit prompt caching. In this post, we use both modes with an open-weight model through the Chat Completions API and show how to read cache usage from each response. We then apply implicit caching to an OpenCode coding agent session on the same API and close with best practices.

articles.title: Mercedes-Benz takes on Tesla FSD with new point-to-point city driving assist
articles.summary:
Mercedes-Benz is tossing its hat into the partial autonomy ring with the launch of two new features next year: hands-free highway driving and a point-to-point city navigation system. The new features will put the German automaker in competition with Tesla, which is currently leading the auto industry in the development of hands-free systems.
Mercedes-Benz takes on Tesla FSD with new point-to-point city driving assist
After pausing its Level 3 system, Mercedes-Benz is rolling out two new Level 2 driver-assistance features in 2027—starting with a California early access program next month.
Mercedes’ point-to-point driver assist feature, called MB.Drive Assist Pro, will handle most of the driving on local roads and in dense, urban traffic. Once a destination is plugged into the vehicle’s navigation, the system assists across the entire route, handling highway exits, lane changes, intersections, and traffic lights. But unlike Tesla’s Full Self-Driving, MB.Drive Assist Pro requires that drivers keep their hands on the wheel while navigating through cities.
The system is powered by 27 sensors (10 cameras, 5 radars, 12 ultrasonic sensors) and a high-performance computer capable of 254 TOPS running on the new MB.OS architecture. That computer runs on Nvidia’s Drive AV stack, blending pure AI with a deterministic “Halos” safety guardrail layer. articles.title: The small African lab sounding the alarm on AI bioweapons
articles.summary:
Out of curiosity, researchers at a small artificial intelligence lab in Accra, Ghana, removed the guardrails on their drug discovery AI model in 2024. They asked it to design toxins instead.
The model produced designs for 1,020 proteins and 5,000 small molecules. The researchers never made any of them in a lab, but software that predicts how poisonous a substance is scored all of them as likely toxic. Some of them resembled ricin, a deadly poison. The study was uploaded to the preprint server arXiv in May 2025.
“We were all shocked,” Darlington Akogo, founder of MinoHealth AI Labs, told Rest of World.
For Akogo, the results also raised a new question: If someone took designs like these to a company that makes DNA to order, would anyone stop them?
Across Africa, the need to regulate DNA synthesis providers is now echoing through the highest levels of government, Brenda Obuya, a senior official at Kenya’s Ministry of Information, Communications and the Digital Economy, told Rest of World.
Akogo has traveled the world warning that AI poses an existential bioweapons threat. He discussed it on the sidelines of the World Bank Group and International Monetary Fund Spring Meetings held in Washington, D.C., last year. He discussed the broader risk over dinner with Microsoft co-founder Bill Gates in 2023, whom he described as “on the fence” at the time. articles.title: Tor Updates DoS Defenses Again as Relay Attacks Continue
articles.summary:
The Tor Project has released new security fixes for its core software as a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack continues to strain the volunteer-run relays that make up its network.
Tor 0.4.9.17, announced on November 13, patches several security issues. The project singled out one fix related to how relays’ built-in DoS protections deal with IPv6.
“This release comes in rapid response to the ongoing DDoS attack on the network, which has affected most relay operators. This is not an easy problem to address, as relays across the network are being overwhelmed by a massive flood of client circuits,” Tor developer David Goulet said in the announcement.
According to the project, more defenses are under consideration, and new versions should follow shortly. Anyone running a relay has been urged to update without delay.
The latest version comes less than three weeks after Tor 0.4.9.15, which introduced three DoS protections against what the project described as a “thunderstorm” of directory requests.
Writing to relay operators at the time, Goulet noted that a single relay could be hit with hundreds of circuits per second. He cautioned that relays would remain under heavy load for as long as the attack lasted.

La directora financiera, Colette Kress, es desde entonces la directora ejecutiva interina y mantiene su cargo anterior. El directorio busca un sucesor. La empresa informó que el informe y la conferencia con inversionistas se harán en la fecha prevista.

Las opciones, contratos con los que los inversionistas apuestan a la dirección de una acción, anticipan un movimiento de alrededor de 9,1% en el precio tras el informe, en cualquier sentido, según Benzinga.

articles.title: A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
articles.summary:
A tiny supercurrent could unlock quantum information without destroying it
Scientists have developed a promising new method that could read quantum information with 99.85% accuracy while barely disturbing the qubit itself.
- Date:
- November 4, 2026
- Source:
- Fundação de Amparo à Pesquisa do Estado de São Paulo
- Summary:
- Researchers have proposed a breakthrough technique for reading quantum information without destroying the delicate states that make quantum computers work. By detecting an electrical signal generated by the qubit itself, their method achieved up to 99.85% accuracy in simulations and could make future quantum computers simpler and more efficient.
- Share:
One of the biggest obstacles in quantum computing is surprisingly simple to describe: how do you read information without changing or destroying it? Unlike the bits used in ordinary computers, quantum bits, or qubits, are extraordinarily sensitive to measurement. Trying to determine their state can cause that state to collapse, potentially erasing the very information scientists want to retrieve.
Researchers have now proposed a way to overcome much of this difficulty by using an unusual electrical signal produced by the qubit itself. Their approach focuses on a special type known as an "Andreev qubit," which can generate an oscillating electric supercurrent through its own quantum behavior. By monitoring this current, scientists may be able to determine the qubit's state without directly measuring it or …

Agents are emerging as reusable design tools, but trust and use models remain challenging.
Key Takeaways:
AI agents are emerging as a new category of reusable design capability, but with a twist. Rather than providing tightly defined design blocks, agents can be used to explore different options, integrate them, and use those changes to improve designs.
At the leading edge, soft IP developers have been customizing their code for large customers for more than a decade to boost performance and/or reduce power. But that customization is typically narrow and costly, and optimizations for one design may not directly transfer to derivative chips — especially multi-die assemblies at the leading edge.
Agents, in contrast, can be used to customize different functions with little or no human intervention, and they can self-optimize for different workloads and use cases, and some agents can even adjust for aging hardware. And they can do all of this much faster than a human, even though an experienced engineering team is needed to verify those results and recommendations.

articles.title: Can Indonesian researchers ever win a Nobel? Not without overhauling the research ecosystem

Will Indonesia ever win the Nobel Prize? That question probably pops into some Indonesians’ minds whenever Nobel season starts in October.
The reality is that there are no shortcuts to a Nobel. Breakthroughs recognised by the committee almost always stem from foundational work done decades earlier — often when it is impossible to foresee the practical payoffs.
Take the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine awarded to Peter Hegemann, Georg Nagel and Karl Deisseroth for pioneering optogenetics — a breakthrough technique that uses light to control nerve cell activity.
Read more: Bagaimana alga mengantarkan ilmuwan pada Nobel Kedokteran dan cara baru memahami otak
Interestingly, the road to optogenetics began with research that seemed to have nothing to do with medicine. Hegemann was initially investigating how the single-celled green alga Chlamydomonas swims towards light. His collaboration with Nagel eventually led to the discovery of channelrhodopsin — a light-sensitive protein that acts as an ion channel.
By 2005, Deisseroth’s team showed that channelrhodopsin could be harnessed to control neuronal firing with light. What began as a humble inquiry into pond algae laid the groundwork for optogenetics — now an indispensable tool for mapping and manipulating the brain.
This trajectory illustrates the road to the prestigious award: Nobel-worthy breakthroughs emerge from ecosystems patient enough to let basic research mature before demanding immediate benefits.

articles.title: A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
articles.summary:
A hidden limit of space and time could unlock electronics 100,000 times faster
- Date:
- November 7, 2026
- Source:
- University of Regensburg
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a surprising quantum limit that prevents electrons from being tracked with unlimited precision in both space and time. The breakthrough could pave the way for manipulating chemical reactions and developing electronics hundreds of thousands of times faster than today's technology.
- Share:
Quantum physics places fundamental limits on what scientists can know about the behavior of particles. Werner Heisenberg's famous uncertainty principle states that certain properties, such as a particle's position and momentum, cannot both be measured with unlimited precision. This restriction is not caused by flaws in scientific instruments. It is built into the laws of nature.
But position and time are different. Heisenberg's uncertainty principle does not impose the same restriction on these quantities. Now, researchers have experimentally demonstrated another fundamental limitation: an electron's location and its behavior over time cannot both be determined with arbitrary precision. Known as the "space-time limit," this newly observed relationship could have major implications for the future of quantum technology and ultrafast electronics.

articles.title: New NoisyTCP vulnerability lets attackers crash Linux servers
articles.summary:
An 11-year-old Linux kernel vulnerability, dubbed NoisyTCP, affects almost all Linux distributions and lets attackers crash systems running Nginx, Apache, and SSH servers with default configurations.
According to Hyunwoo Kim, the security researcher who discovered it, this pre-authenticated remote corruption flaw (tracked as CVE-2026-99288) stems from a NULL pointer dereference weakness in the Linux kernel's TCP networking subsystem.
Unauthenticated attackers can trigger it remotely via maliciously crafted TCP packets that exploit the timing between SYN cookie handling and socket hashing to crash the kernel and operating system on targeted servers.
However, while CVE-2026-99288 exploits cause a kernel panic and take down the host, they don't allow threat actors to alter data or gain arbitrary code execution.
Kim added that although attackers can exploit this vulnerability against any Linux system that receives TCP packets directly and runs Nginx, Apache, or an SSH server, "the race window is narrow, so triggering it against a quiet bare-metal server can take a long time."
"Due to a race condition during lockless socket lookups, recycled socket memory can be accessed before it is properly initialized and hashed. A remote attacker could exploit this issue by generating network traffic that drives socket reuse, triggering a NULL pointer dereference and kernel crash that results in a Denial of Service (DoS)," the Red Hat security team explained.

articles.title: Helping AI coding agents work smarter, for less
articles.summary:
At a glance
- Developers use AI coding agents in the same codebases day after day, yet agents often start each session from scratch: rediscovering familiar facts, loading unused tools, and repeating unsuccessful approaches.
- TokenEconomizer is an open-source plugin that learns from an agent’s past sessions in a repository to reduce waste in future sessions, without modifying the agent or its underlying model.
- Across 277 real bug-fixing tasks, TokenEconomizer reduced costs by 18.4–30.9% across multiple AI coding agents. Costs fell in every repository tested, while task success rates remained broadly stable.
AI coding agents are increasingly helping developers fix bugs and build features largely on their own, but every interaction with their models consumes tokens. In each session, an agent sends instructions, tool descriptions, and session history to its model. Most efforts to reduce this cost focus on individual tasks. Yet developers return to the same repositories, giving agents an opportunity to learn from previous work. Without that learning, an agent may repeatedly rediscover how to run tests, load tools it never uses, or spend dozens of turns revisiting the same error.
In our paper, TokenEconomizer: Experience-Driven Black-Box Cost Control for Coding Agents, we ask a simple question: can experience in a repository help an agent solve future tasks more efficiently? Obtaining clear images of gaps and delaminations in advanced packages.
We all know how important inspection is for advanced packaging. Not only are these processes critical for ensuring higher yield, but they’re also integral for maintaining device reliability. As the industry pushes for smaller features and tighter spacing, even the smallest defects can pose major challenges. For instance, delaminations and air gaps can be detrimental in a market that demands increasingly complex devices. Such defects will lead to electrical or mechanical failures down the road.
One technology that’s mitigating these issues is acoustic micro imaging (AMI). AMI is a high-frequency ultrasound technology, and it’s being used by the industry as an inspection method.
At the core of AMI technology is a transducer, or a device that turns energy from one form to another. It starts with a pulse of electrical energy, then converts it to mechanical energy, or a high-frequency ultrasound wave. Because ultrasound doesn’t travel through air, this allows inspectors to obtain clear images of gaps and delaminations in the device that could otherwise be difficult to see.
However, the transducers used for AMI are not all the same. Each transducer handles a specific frequency, and they’re chosen based on the sample that needs to be inspected. Curious Kids is a series for children of all ages. If you have a question you’d like an expert to answer, send it to CuriousKidsUS@theconversation.com.
Why does your body store fat in your butt? - Ellen, age 8, Cambridge, Massachusetts
Have you ever wondered why some parts of your body are firm, like your elbows, while other areas, like your butt, are squishier?
The difference is due to what scientists call fat distribution, and researchers are still trying to understand why bodies store fat in some places but not in others.
All animals have fat in their bodies, even insects. Bears even put on up to 400 pounds (180 kilograms) of additional body fat, the equivalent of 544 large cheese pizzas, to survive hibernation.
Fat is an important and constantly changing part of all bodies, including those of humans and our evolutionary ancestors.
What is fat?
Fat, also called adipose tissue, is one kind of connective tissue that helps hold your body together.
For a long time, scientists thought that adipose tissue was mainly a storage place for the extra energy your body doesn’t use from the food you eat. While fat is a great source of stored energy, it also has many other functions. There are even different kinds of fat.

articles.title: League of Legends: Nova Alvorada reformula mapa e client em 2027
articles.summary:
League of Legends: Nova Alvorada é a atualização do LoL prevista para 2027 que promete reformular Summoner’s Rift, modernizar o client e trazer melhorias de jogabilidade. A Riot Games apresentou a novidade no sábado (14), durante a final do Campeonato Mundial de League of Legends, o Worlds 2026.
Chamada de New Dawn em inglês, a atualização reúne mudanças no visual, no mapa e nas formas de jogar com os campeões. A desenvolvedora divulgou um teaser com uma prévia das novidades.
O que muda no LoL com a atualização Nova Alvorada?
A Nova Alvorada prevê mudanças em diferentes partes de League of Legends, da interface usada para acessar o jogo às partidas em Summoner’s Rift. Entre as novidades anunciadas estão:
- Client modernizado;
- Reformulação visual e do mapa de Summoner’s Rift;
- Melhorias de jogabilidade;
- Novas formas de jogar com os campeões.
O client é a interface pela qual os jogadores acessam recursos e iniciam partidas. Já Summoner’s Rift é o principal mapa competitivo do LoL e também receberá mudanças com a atualização.
A Riot apresentou uma prévia no teaser de League of Legends: Nova Alvorada. Os detalhes sobre o funcionamento das novidades ainda não foram divulgados.
Quando League of Legends: Nova Alvorada será lançado?
O lançamento de League of Legends: Nova Alvorada está previsto para 2027. Por enquanto, a Riot Games não anunciou dia ou mês para a chegada da atualização.

articles.title: US tightens AI chip export controls to deter Chinese companies from accessing compute remotely | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The Trump administration on Monday is preparing to roll out new export controls on AI chips and data centers outside the U.S., seeking to prevent companies, especially those in China, from getting past U.S. export controls by remotely accessing AI infrastructure located in other countries.
Under the interim rule, the Commerce Department will require companies to get licenses to export, reexport, or transfer AI chips and servers to data centers anywhere in the world if they may provide compute to companies in China or other restricted countries.
The remote-access rules target companies based in the U.S.’s D:5 group of embargoed countries, which includes China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and 18 others.
The U.S. already has rules requiring chip companies to get a license to ship AI chips to companies based in, or owned by any business in, this group of countries.
“This new control is a logical extension of existing controls,” the interim rule reads. “These restrictions will undermine the ability of companies headquartered in countries of concern from using U.S. advanced Super Intelligence (SI) semiconductors to train advanced SI models.”
The move comes days after Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned amid a scandal involving an alleged Chinese spy linked to one of the chipmaker’s customers. articles.title: Hackers Probe Newly Disclosed Flaws in Copeland Refrigeration Controllers
articles.summary:
Exploitation attempts against a vulnerability in Copeland’s XWEB EVO refrigeration controllers began less than two hours after the issue was made public last week, according to VulnCheck.
The security firm disclosed 14 vulnerabilities in XWEB EVO, a Dixell supervisory system now sold under the Copeland name. VulnCheck’s Valentin Lobstein said each flaw was shown to yield root privileges on test systems.
The product drew the researcher’s attention after the October 11-12 attack that triggered defrost cycles at roughly 700 French supermarkets. CERT-FR named Copeland and Dixell XWEB controllers among the compromised products, and France has blamed Iran for the campaign.
Nine of the flaws disclosed by VulnCheck only affect firmware builds that predate a 2021 rewrite. They include unauthenticated command execution, a hardcoded administrator password, and command injection via the login page.
The other five vulnerabilities also impact the latest firmware. Four of them involve predictable credentials: the administrator’s daily password is generated from the device’s MAC address and the current date, and the MAC address is exposed to unauthenticated users.
An attacker can calculate the password offline, enable SSH, and log in as root, since the root password is built from the same daily code. The fifth flaw is a command injection issue that requires authentication.
These five issues will not be fixed. Copeland ended software support for the XWEB EVO family on March 16, 2026, and has …

articles.title: Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Best practices for writing Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails
With Denied Topics in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, you block a content category by describing it in plain language, and the guardrail applies that description to every request by meaning rather than by keyword. That same mechanism can also match more than you intend. A topic named Finance, meant to keep an assistant out of investment advice, also blocks “When does my direct deposit clear?”. Inputs close in meaning to the topic can get caught, not only the requests you intended.
When Denied Topics blocks too much or too little, the cause is usually one of four authoring patterns:
- Topics that block legitimate queries. A topic framed around a subject domain (Finance, Legal, Compensation) rather than the user’s intention can match queries semantically near that domain. This is a frequent failure mode.
- Topics that miss the requests they were written to catch. A definition built from keyword lists (“words like invest, portfolio, stock…”) misses phrasings that use other vocabulary and fires on unrelated inputs that happen to share those words.
- Examples that teach the wrong thing. Five paraphrases of one idea leave the topic’s boundaries unguarded, and examples that name specific countries, products, or companies pull those entities into the topic’s context.
- Topics that interfere with each other. Overlapping definitions compete for the same input, report matches inconsistently, and can…

Inside this quantum computer, memory vibrates like a guitar string

- Source:

The breakthrough successfully demonstrated advanced quantum calculations and could help overcome major barriers to practical quantum computing.
- Share:
A quantum computer might seem to have little in common with a guitar, but researchers at ETH Zurich have found a surprising connection. Physicist Yiwen Chu and her team have developed a system that uses microscopic mechanical vibrations to store and manipulate quantum information, much like the vibrating strings of a guitar produce musical notes.
Unlike the sounds produced by a musical instrument, these vibrations occur at frequencies far beyond human hearing. They take place within a tiny quantum chip, where they serve as a new form of computer memory.
By harnessing these vibrations, the researchers have created a way for quantum computers to process information efficiently while accessing a flexible working memory. "The interaction between the quantum processor and the quantum memory provides a crucial foundation with a view to establishing quantum computers as a powerful and reliable way to perform computations that are not feasible with conventional computers," says Yiwen Chu.

articles.title: Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?
articles.summary:
Can Robots Bring Stroke Surgery to Remote Hospitals?
Remedy Robotics is testing whether surgeons can operate from afar
I am practicing brain surgery on a patient lying 6 meters away, out of my sight and reach. I press a foot pedal, activating the controller in my hand, and carefully steer a thin flexible tube called a catheter up through the patient’s blood vessels. I head for what I believe to be the brain, tracking my progress on the live X-ray feed. As I imagine finding a blood clot, David Bell, the surgeon seated to my right, helpfully reminds me that every minute a stroke goes untreated, millions of brain cells suffocate, swell, and die.
The patient under the X-ray in Bell’s office is not flesh and blood, but a plastic container holding long branches of silicone tubing. The controller I hold comes from an Xbox. But the surgical robot is real. The Remedy N1 is designed for emergency operations, including thrombectomies, the standard brain operation for acute ischemic strokes caused by blood clots. Ischemia, a restriction of blood flow, is the most common cause of stroke.
“We want it to feel a bit like a video game—a bit easy,” Bell says. “But we don’t want to dehumanize it as if there’s just another ‘game over.’ ” Bell, a clinician and former cardiac-surgery trainee from Australia, cofounded Remedy Robotics, based in San Francisco. articles.title: Hay una guerra que no necesita soldados ni misiles: Europa está descubriendo cómo funciona la guerra híbrida
articles.summary:
Europa lleva un mes sufriendo ataques contra lo más cotidiano: los frigoríficos de varias cadenas de supermercados que llegaron a 50 grados. Un banco de sangre francés vio manipulados sus congeladores, y las falsas bombas pusieron en alerta aviones y escuelas.
Por separado estos incidentes pueden parecer fruto de ciberataques aislados, pero si se analizan en conjunto empieza a aparecer un patrón que converge en una serie de países. La pregunta es si hay una guerra híbrida detrás, qué busca esa presión en suelo europeo y a quién beneficia. Dos hipótesis ganan peso: la IA como acelerador y una coordinación interesada por encima de cada ataque.
Cómo funciona una guerra híbrida. Guido Crosetto, ministro de Defensa italiano, describió una guerra que se libra "por debajo del umbral". Su objetivo es ofuscar el origen del ataque de forma que cueste señalar a un claro culpable del ataque, de forma que no existe una agresión directa, sino un ataque no reivindicado. Son golpes lo bastante pequeños para no justificar una respuesta militar, pero diseñados para ser repetidos y desgastar al gobierno de los países atacados provocando caos y malestar entre la población.
Tal y como señalan en Foreign Policy, su arma más valiosa es la asimetría. Solo se necesitan unos minutos para generar un correo electrónico falso y ofuscar su origen, pero obliga al objetivo a evacuar aeropuertos, desviar aviones o movilizar cazas. articles.title: Anatomy of a CPU
articles.summary:
The CPU is often called the brains of a computer, and just like the human brain, it consists of several parts that work together to process information. Some take information in, some store it, some process it, and others send the results back out. In today's explainer, we'll go over the key elements that make up a CPU and how they all work together to power your computer.
This article is part of our Anatomy series, which dissects the tech behind every major PC component. If you want to go even deeper, our CPU Design series covers how processors are designed and built in much more technical detail. This article goes over some of those fundamentals at a higher level and brings them up to date with how modern CPUs actually work.
Compared to other articles in our Anatomy series (see the full list of hardware components below), this one will inevitably be more abstract.
When you're looking inside something like a power supply, you can clearly see the capacitors, transformers, and other components. That's simply not possible with a modern CPU since everything is so tiny and because chipmakers like Intel, AMD, Apple and Qualcomm only share their designs at a high level. The actual circuitry is proprietary, so the topics covered in this article represent the general features that all CPUs have.

articles.title: Los grandes centros de datos de EE UU ya consumen tanta energía como todo Chile
articles.summary:
Los grandes centros de datos de EE UU ya consumen tanta energía como todo Chile
Un estudio publicado en Nature estima que estas infraestructuras acaparan el 1,8% de la electricidad del país y que las emisiones de carbono se han triplicado desde 2018
Los centros de datos son la columna vertebral de la era digital. En estas instalaciones repletas de procesadores se computan, almacenan y distribuyen ingentes cantidades de datos que hacen posible los servicios online o la inteligencia artificial (IA). Precisamente el boom de la IA ha provocado un frenesí constructor de centros de datos. Tenerlos en marcha día y noche requiere de muchísima energía, que se usa tanto para alimentar las propias máquinas como para refrigerarlas. Pero, ¿cuánta? ¿Y cuál es su huella de carbono?
La respuesta a estas preguntas solo las conocen las propias empresas que operan los centros de datos. No hay información pública y transparente al respecto. La opacidad de la industria hace que las cifras que se manejan sean estimaciones elaboradas por la comunidad científica. Un grupo de investigadores liderado por la Universidad de Harvard publica este lunes en la revista Nature los resultados de sus propias pesquisas, centradas en los hiperescalares (así se llama a los centros de datos más grandes). El estudio se fija en EE UU, el país del mundo que aglutina más centros de datos, en torno a la mitad del total.

articles.title: Anthropic’s Claude Fable 5.2 blocks fewer security tasks, while Mythos gets better at finding bugs
articles.summary:
Anthropic recently rolled out Claude Mythos 5.2 to selected partners and Fable 5.2 to regular users, with improvements to coding and reasoning. But we also noticed some interesting cybersecurity changes.
Anthropic describes Mythos 5.2 as its "most capable model for cybersecurity engineering," which means it's now ahead of Fable 5.2 in security research.
However, that doesn't mean Fable 5.2 misses out on security restrictions, as it does come with cybersecurity safeguards, which block most potentially dangerous hacking activities.
According to Anthropic, Mythos 5.2 beats Fable 5.2 at finding vulnerabilities, reproducing them, and developing fixes. This makes sense, as Mythos is designed for organizations working on advanced cybersecurity tasks.
The company also shared some numbers. For example, Anthropic's CVE Rediscovery evaluation found that the Mythos 5.2 model can detect 10.2% more vulnerabilities than Claude Opus 5.5 and 14.4% more than Mythos 5.1.
Moreover, a security company told Anthropic that "one in six confirmed bugs" identified by Mythos 5.2 had been missed by every other frontier model it tested.
Claude Fable 5.2 blocks most high-risk cybersecurity tasks
Although Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are based on the same underlying parent model, there are obvious differences, and it's totally due to their intended use cases.
Unlike Mythos, Anthropic applied additional cybersecurity and biology safeguards to Fable so it can be made available to regular users.

articles.title: Los despedidos de trabajos expuestos a la IA tardan un mes más en reemplazarse, según un informe
articles.summary:
Los trabajadores despedidos de empleos expuestos a la inteligencia artificial (IA) desde 2025 tardaron cerca de un mes más en encontrar otro trabajo que el resto de los despedidos. Así lo concluyó el banco Goldman Sachs en una nota publicada el 29 de octubre, según informó Fortune.
El economista del banco Pierfrancesco Mei también halló que esos trabajadores tenían unos 10 puntos porcentuales más de probabilidad de seguir sin empleo un año después de perderlo. Mei calificó esos efectos como “comparables en magnitud” a los de olas tecnológicas anteriores, cuyo daño describió como “duradero”.

articles.title: Veterano do Linux reduz atividades no projeto por causa da IA • Tecnoblog
articles.summary:
Veterano do Linux reduz atividades no projeto por causa da IA
Responsável por áreas de gerenciamento de memória no Linux, Lorenzo Stoakes decidiu reduzir sua participação no kernel por causa da sobrecarga oriunda da IA.
Meses atrás, quando Linus Torvalds sinalizou que a IA estava sobrecarregando os desenvolvedores do Linux, ele não estava exagerando. Prova disso é que, recentemente, Lorenzo Stoakes decidiu reduzir a sua presença no projeto. É uma decisão impactante. Estamos falando do responsável por cuidar de quatro áreas relacionadas ao gerenciamento de memória do kernel.
O problema não é a inteligência artificial por si só. O ponto de conflito está no uso de ferramentas que “caçam bugs” no Linux com auxílio da IA e, principalmente, nos códigos gerados por elas. Em linhas gerais, esses mecanismos têm produzido um volume muito grande de relatórios de falhas e sugestões de patches, a ponto de os desenvolvedores terem dificuldade para lidar com tudo isso.
Talvez a pior parte seja o fato de boa parte desses relatórios ou patches estarem relacionados a bugs com baixa de prioridade, que já estavam na fila de correção ou até que foram corrigidos recentemente.
Mas, sim, a IA também tem conseguido apontar problemas ou pontos de ajustes legítimos, mas em um ritmo com o qual os desenvolvedores do Linux não estavam habituados. Ao que tudo indica, foi isso que fez Stoakes reduzir a sua participação no projeto.

articles.title: China encendió la turbina eólica marina más grande del mundo y se da cuenta de que influye hasta en el clima
articles.summary:
Hace un tiempo, China conectó a la red la turbina eólica marina de Mingyang Smart Energy MySE18.X-20MW. Se trataba de la turbina de mayor potencia unitaria y rotor más grande del mundo, según la propia compañía. Los estudios citados no acreditan que haya supuesto cambios inesperados en el microclima de la zona.
Se ha instalado en Hainan. La plataforma soporta hasta 20 megavatios. El diámetro del rotor de la plataforma va de 260 a 292 metros. De acuerdo con la comunicación de la empresa, el área barrida por las palas llega a ser de 66.966 metros cuadrados.
En su informe de sostenibilidad de 2024 estiman la producción (con una velocidad media de viento de 8,5 m/s) hasta en 80 gigavatios hora/año. Es decir, el equivalente al consumo de unas 96.000 personas en un año.
Qué ocurre con el aire que atraviesa un parque eólico
Los aerogeneradores aprovechan la energía del viento. Como consecuencia, crean estelas. Estas estelas están a sotavento (dirección de propagación del viento). En ellas se reduce la velocidad y aumenta la turbulencia. El alcance de estas estelas depende de las condiciones atmosféricas y de cómo se dispongan las máquinas.
Astrid Lampert y colaboradores han publicado un trabajo en agosto de 2026 en la revista Wind Energy Science donde analizan medidas en parques marinos de la bahía alemana. Han realizado mediciones en altura. Se describen estelas que pueden llegar a decenas de km (si hay una atmósfera estable). También se producen cambios de temperatura y de humedad…

articles.summary:
Google a déployé une nouvelle version de Chrome. Disponible depuis ce mercredi 11 novembre sur Windows, macOS et Linux, la mise à jour corrige un total de 83 failles de sécurité. C’est la deuxième mise à jour de sécurité en une semaine. Deux jours plus tôt, Google avait déjà corrigé en urgence une faille zero day exploitée par des pirates. C’était la huitième faille zero day de l’année découverte sur le navigateur.
Cinq failles critiques dans la mémoire de Chrome
Parmi les 83 brèches, cinq ont été jugées « critiques », le niveau de gravité le plus élevé, par les ingénieurs de Google. Les 78 autres sont de sévérité « élevée ». Cette fois, Google n’a pas découvert de tentative d’exploitation des failles. Les cinq failles critiques concernent la gestion de la mémoire. Concrètement, Chrome libère une zone de la mémoire, mais continue ensuite de s’en servir. Un pirate peut alors glisser des données malveillantes dans cet espace. Les chercheurs de Malwarebytes soulignent que ce problème de mémoire peut provoquer des « plantages, des corruptions de données et des fuites d’informations ».
L’une des failles de sévérité a déjà retenu l’attention des cybercriminels. Située dans V8, le moteur qui exécute le code JavaScript des sites web, elle « permet à un attaquant distant d’exécuter du code arbitraire à l’intérieur du bac à sable de Chrome via une page HTML spécialement conçue », explique Google. articles.summary:
Darum erstrahlte ein unscheinbarer Komet plötzlich tausendfach heller als normal
Der Komet 220P/McNaught hat im vergangenen Sommer für Aufsehen in der Astronomie-Welt gesorgt. Aufgrund der Hitze der Sonne wandelte sich Eis unter seiner Oberfläche zu Gas um – und als Folge wurden bis zu 50 Milliarden Kilogramm Staub in den Weltraum geschleudert. Das führte dazu, dass der Komet plötzlich tausendmal heller erstrahlte.
Der beobachtete Komet ist eigentlich unscheinbar
Bei 220P/McNaught handelt es sich um einen periodischen Kometen. Sprich: einem regelmäßig zurückkehrenden. Im Fall von 220P geschieht dies alle fünfeinhalb Jahre, wenn er der Sonne etwa so nahe kommt wie der Mars. Generell ist dieser Komet laut Space unscheinbar. Normalerweise ist er so lichtschwach, dass er für die meisten Amateur-Teleskope nicht zu erkennen ist.
Das änderte sich im Juni und Juli 2026. Während er sich auf den sonnennächsten Punkt seiner Umlaufbahn zubewegte, erwachte 220P plötzlich und völlig unerwartet zu neuem Leben und strahlte viel heller als zuvor.
Die Staubpartikel breiteten sich extrem schnell aus
Zum Hintergrund: Kometen werden oft als „schmutzige Schneebälle“ bezeichnet. Unter ihrer staubigen Kruste verbergen sich Eisvorkommen aus verschiedenen flüchtigen Stoffen, darunter Wasser, Kohlendioxid und Stickstoff. Researchers communicate complex scientific hypotheses in natural language and let autonomous agents independently plan tasks, execute simulations, evaluate results, and self-correct across multiple iterations. Accuracy and inference efficiency matter at every step. Without verification, errors compound across the workflow, while latency and compute costs multiply with continued operation.
NVIDIA Nemotron for Science, a collection of models, datasets, tools, and recipes for accelerating agentic scientific workloads, addresses these hurdles. It includes Nemotron 3.5 Super VL—an open, customizable, multimodal model for these specialized workflows—and the NVIDIA Nemotron Litmus-Bench V2.0, an open source chemistry-reasoning dataset and benchmark that was designed to train and evaluate LLMs and agentic AI models on molecular properties. articles.title: Audible turns to AI to help users discover audiobooks | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
Amazon-owned audiobook service Audible is turning to AI to help listeners find their next book. The company on Monday launched a new “audio discovery” feature that provides a brief overview of a book’s themes and a summary of what readers liked about it, as well as commentary from an Audible editor or an author, in addition to playing the narrated sample.
The overview audio itself is generated using AI, and the commentary is pulled from recordings of past Audible interviews, the company says.
The idea is that this type of expanded introduction to a story could help users decide what to listen to next, particularly when they’re on the go and don’t have time to scroll through comments or reviews.
The feature follows last month’s launch of a handful of AI tools that let users engage more with the story, interact with characters, or catch up with the help of recaps. These features have come as Audible faces new competition in the audiobooks market, namely from Spotify, which introduced audiobook listening hours as part of its paid subscriptions. That service expanded last month to over 180 markets.
Audible’s new feature takes a cue from how Amazon is already using AI to help people shop: On the Amazon storefront, AI can summarize buyers’ product reviews so shoppers can get a quick sense of what people had to say, as well as the pros and cons of a particular item. In Audible’s case, it’s pulling information about what people liked about the book from publicly available reviews.

articles.title: NVIDIA Expands Slurm to Bring Quantum Computing Into Supercomputing
articles.summary:
Quantum processor deployments at supercomputing centers have grown nearly sevenfold over the past five years, with nearly 30 supercomputing centers around the world now in the process of deploying over 50 quantum processors.
Many of these centers use Slurm to run scientific supercomputing workloads, so expanding its support for quantum processors builds on familiar workflows and tools, enabling computational chemists, nuclear physicists and materials scientists to bring quantum computing into their research domains without friction.
In a new release, Slurm builds on previous work with IBM, Pasqal and the wider quantum computing community to allow QPU builders to create a single interface to their hardware for every supercomputing center, through a simple file. This makes it easier than ever for HPC centers and QPU builders to integrate and serve their hardware.
The expansion is already being adopted by Alice & Bob, IBM, IQM, Pasqal, Quantinuum and MQSC and supports the widely used QRMI and QDMI interfaces.
Beating the Bottleneck
Until now, integrating a QPU into a supercomputing center meant a new software challenge for every new QPU or supercomputing center. By building on existing quantum-HPC interfaces such as QRMI and QDMI, the Slurm expansion allows QPU builders to reuse their integrations across all their deployments. articles.title: Security patches are supposed to protect you. Google found AI agents turning them into exploits.

Google’s Threat Intelligence Group says attackers are using autonomous AI agents to reverse-engineer security patches, generate exploits, and attempt to execute them without human approval.
In a report published Monday, Google and Mandiant describe the first cases their researchers have identified of attackers using LLM frameworks to fully automate vulnerability discovery and exploitation.
The framework uses an orchestrator to coordinate specialized agents, share context, and invoke tools through interfaces such as MCP. The agents apply familiar coding workflows to offensive security, identifying vulnerabilities, generating exploit candidates, and testing them against targets.
Inside the exploit pipeline
Google found a publicly exposed staging server running a multi-agent framework called exploit_agent alongside stolen victim data and scripts used after a successful intrusion. The framework connected several frontier and locally hosted language models to automate patch diffing, turning potential vulnerabilities into exploit code that it could then attempt to execute.
The server also contained scripts for reconnaissance, brute-force attacks, installing webshells, and removing those left by competing attackers. articles.title: Recent UnrealIRCd Vulnerability Exploited in Attacks
articles.summary:
Threat actors started exploiting a high-severity vulnerability in the open source Internet Relay Chat (IRC) server UnrealIRCd one day after public disclosure.
Tracked as CVE-2026-114713 (CVSS score: 8.6), the flaw is described as an improper neutralization of delimiters and allows attackers to execute commands with server/IRCOp privileges.
The issue exists because the labeled-response module “does not escape the IRCv3 ‘label’ message tag when echoing it into replies, which allows any user on a network with two or more linked servers to inject server-to-server commands that are executed with server authority,” according to a NIST advisory.
Patches for CVE-2026-114713 and eight other bugs were released on November 7 in UnrealIRCd version 6.2.7.1. A hot patch was also rolled out.
According to UnrealIRCd project leader, developer, and maintainer Bram Matthys, this is the most severe security defect discovered in UnrealIRCd.
“Any ordinary user can KILL, GLINE, and do many more bad things. This is the most critical issue found in UnrealIRCd in the past 15 years,” Matthys said.
Matthys has provided instructions on how to update to UnrealIRCd 6.2.7.1 or apply the hot patch and warned that UnrealIRCd 5 and previous releases have reached End of Life (EoL) and won’t receive a fix.
“It is likely that several bugs that are fixed in 6.2.7.1 go all the way back to 3.2.x,” Matthys said.

articles.title: Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base | Amazon Web Services
articles.summary:
Artificial Intelligence
Get answers from tables with tabular search in Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base
Amazon Bedrock Managed Knowledge Base now supports tabular search, so you can get answers from tables through agentic retrieval. When a question needs data from CSV, XLSX, or XLS files, tabular search looks up values and runs calculations across every relevant row in one or more tables or sheets. It then combines the results with facts from related documents to answer analytical questions that take several steps.
A finance team closing the quarter needs to know “Which departments must write variance commentary?” No single file has the answer. It depends on the variance policy’s threshold, the quarter-close memo’s budget revisions, and math over every department in the profit and loss (P&L) workbook.
Like this finance team, most teams keep their narratives and data in the same place. For example, a Microsoft SharePoint site holds workbooks next to policies, and an Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) bucket holds CSV exports next to PDFs. Tabular search answers questions across these files through the same AgenticRetrieveStream request you already use for documents. It runs code over the original file in an isolated sandbox, so the answer uses the whole table instead of only the rows that retrieval returns. For the finance team, one request returns the departments that must write commentary. The answer cites the policy and the memo, and the trace names the workbook…

articles.title: Beijing now bans owning and storing drones, even if you never fly them
articles.summary:
What just happened? Drone users who complain that rules related to UAVs are too tough should be thankful they don't live in Beijing. A law came into effect in the Chinese capital yesterday that makes owning and storing the devices illegal, meaning you can't even keep a drone that you never fly.
While many Chinese cities have no-fly zones in sensitive areas for civilian drones, Beijing is the only one to ban ownership.
The restrictions cover the entire municipality, including its rural areas, spanning around 16,400 square kilometers (6,332 square miles), around half the size of Belgium. Bringing drones or their components into Beijing is also forbidden, so leaving one packed away in your luggage won't get you around the rules.
Authorities announced the extreme measure in September, claiming it was a requirement to keep the city secure. Beijing had already banned drone sales in May, but registered owners were initially allowed to keep their devices if they registered them with authorities, a luxury that has now disappeared.
In June, a small plane crashed into Beijing's tallest skyscraper, killing the pilot and injuring 13 people. It raised concerns about airspace safety and led to the current drone restrictions.
There are a handful of exemptions that allow drones to be owned and used, including activities involving law enforcement, counterterrorism, emergency relief, agriculture, and scientific research.

articles.title: Hace 2.400 años los poblados del norte de la península se vaciaron en un tiempo récord. Los arqueólogos al fin tienen respuestas
articles.summary:
No sabemos muy bien cómo, ni por qué, pero hacia mediados del primer milenio antes de Cristo ocurrió algo en el norte de la península ibérica: las poblaciones que ocupaban parte de lo que hoy es Galicia, Asturias o Cantabria abandonaron sus asentamientos en un período de tiempo asombrosamente breve, apenas un siglo. El fenómeno pareció arrancar en el occidente cantábrico entre finales del VI e inicios del V a.C. y hacia el IV ya identificamos indicios de la fundación de nuevos poblados, más fortificados y a mayor altura.
Se trata de un fenómeno que conecta con otras regiones del continente, pero todavía hoy sigue siendo un misterio para los expertos. Ahora un estudio aporta algunas respuestas.
“Un punto de inflexión”. Así es como define Samuel Nión-Álvarez, investigador del Instituto de Ciencias del Patrimonio (INCIPIT-CSIC), lo que ocurrió en Europa hacia el 400 a.C., en plena Edad del Hierro: sin que se sepa muy bien cómo ni por qué varias comunidades sufrieron “un cambio de paradigma en su forma de vida”, una “transformación abrupta” que aún intriga a los arqueólogos de 2026.
Al fin y al cabo, insiste Nión-Álvarez en un artículo que acaba de publicar sobre el tema en Journal of Archaeological Science, se trata de “uno de los puntos de inflexión más significativos, pero menos comprendidos”, de toda la prehistoria europea.

articles.title: After a cyberattack, what must Nigerian banks disclose?
articles.summary:
When a bank suffers a cyberattack, its customers care more about the intrusion’s technical details than about the bank. Is their money safe? Has their personal information been exposed? And what should they do to protect themselves?
In Nigeria, the answers depend partly on what happened and partly on who needs to be informed. Reporting an incident to the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) is not the same as notifying affected customers. Neither automatically requires a public announcement. But when a breach of personal data is likely to create a high risk to individuals, the law requires banks to tell those affected.
The distinction has become increasingly important as financial institutions face attacks that can expose customer information, disrupt services or compromise funds. It also raises a difficult question for regulators: how can banks be compelled to disclose incidents without turning every announcement into a threat to public confidence?
CBN figures show that Nigerian banks and their customers lost ₦134.48 billion ($100.09 million) to fraud between 2020 and 2025. The figures cover financial losses suffered by victims, not necessarily money that disappeared from the banking system, and do not distinguish cyberattacks on bank infrastructure from other forms of fraud. More recent data from the Nigerian Interbank Settlement System shows that payment fraud losses fell to ₦25.85 billion ($19.24 million) in 2025, from ₦52.26 billion ($38.90 million) the previous year.

articles.title: Accelerate Molecular Dynamics Simulations with Accurate, Flexible Primitives Using NVIDIA cuPotential | NVIDIA Technical Blog
articles.summary:
Molecular dynamics (MD) is an indispensable tool across physics, chemistry, biology, and materials science. Owing to its arithmetic structure, particularly the parallel evaluation of many atom-pair interactions, MD codes were among the first to be ported to run on GPUs. However, as GPUs evolve, optimizing kernels and ensuring compatibility across heterogeneous hardware have become more difficult than ever for many MD engine developers.
Specifically, in simulations run with classical forcefields, the evaluation of long-range interactions under periodic boundary conditions, such as electrostatics and dispersion, remains the major computational and engineering bottleneck.
NVIDIA cuPotential, a focused library designed for molecular dynamics, addresses these challenges. By offering modular primitives with a C API, cuPotential empowers developers and users to select specific components from multiple layers of the stack to accelerate workloads (Figure 1).

articles.title: The Sound of Smarter Farming - EE Times
articles.summary:
It was amid the stillness of the Covid-19 lockdowns that Conrad Young, founder and CEO of Chirrup.ai, realized that birdsong would make an excellent proxy for biodiversity. Birds have always acted as sentinels for changes in the environment, and as he told EE Times, “Birdsong is a pretty powerful and visceral way of understanding what’s going on in the environment but is also scientifically valid and benchmarkable.”
In March 2022, as the pandemic ended, Young launched Chirrup.ai to monitor birdsong and track farmland diversity. The first task was to deploy acoustic sensors and establish a baseline of bird activity that could provide a reference point against future recordings and reveal whether biodiversity was improving, declining, or remaining stable over time. Earlier trials used audiomoths—low-cost, acoustic loggers that record birdsong—but Chirrup.ai has now developed smart acoustic sensors.
The sensor pairs a MEMS analog microphone with a 24-bit digital audio codec, a 240-MHz processor with Bluetooth, and a high-speed 4G LTE modem. A multi-constellation GNSS receiver supporting GPS, GLONASS, and Galileo provides geolocation and timestamping for the acoustic data. The device is powered by a rechargeable lithium-polymer battery.

To train an AI model, thousands of GPUs have to work together, requiring a network that’s fast, efficient and resilient.
Lambda is tackling the network piece of the puzzle with NVIDIA Photonics co-packaged optics (CPO) switches. The cloud provider is using the switches to connect NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 racks with more than 10,000 GPUs, delivering lower power, higher resiliency and longer mean time between interruptions (MTBI) to an AI factory at scale.
“Networking has to keep pace with the demands of increasingly large AI clusters,” said Dave Ward, president of cloud services at Lambda. “Bringing co-packaged optics into a deployment of this scale is an important step toward building the infrastructure needed to support the next generation of AI.”
In the company’s tests using the switches, network latency — the time needed for moving data — dropped by about 4% at rack scale and by up to about 10% at pod scale. Across rack, scalable unit and pod configurations, the network maintains the same throughput as conventional pluggable optics.
Delivering Power Efficiency and Resiliency at Scale
Improving power efficiency and resiliency matters because the network sits at the center of AI factory productivity.
In a large training job, one interrupted link can stall thousands of GPUs. With agentic inference, one network disruption can introduce cascading latency effects on many agents. Every interruption costs time, and every watt spent on networking is a watt not available for compute.

The original definition of "hacking" was making hardware and software do something it wasn't supposed to.
Hacking stories these days mostly involve someone using an army of AI agents to find vulnerabilities in networks and software that were carefully hidden in plain sight. Today, for a change, we have a story about hacking in its original meaning — twisting computing artifacts into purposes not in their design spec. David Oberhollenzer, aka Goliath, a greybeard in spirit if not in shade, crafted a 100% valid ZIP file that's simultaneously an archive, BIOS-bootable, and a Multiboot-compatible OS image.
You can unpack the ZIP file just like any other, boot it using Linux's GRUB, QEMU, or any other Multiboot-compatible loader (even if imaged to different media), or alternatively, perform the finest party trick: image-write it to a floppy and boot from it directly from BIOS on any compatible PC, without modification.
Much like me, that sequence of words may be triggering a head-tilt reminiscent of a confused puppy, so we'll explain. The first thing you need to know is that unlike most file types, the metadata (in this case, file directory) of a ZIP is actually at the end of the archive. articles.title: Alpine Linux Users Urged to Patch OpenSSH Authentication Flaw
articles.summary:
A recently disclosed vulnerability in OpenSSH lets an unauthenticated attacker log into accounts that should have no usable password. The issue, named *sshole and tracked as CVE-2026-123158, affects Linux systems running OpenSSH with the musl C library and which don't use PAM. Security researchers now report that attackers are exploiting it in the wild.
The flaw comes from the way OpenSSH checks passwords when musl handles the underlying crypt() call. On an affected system, a password longer than 256 bytes causes musl to return an error value. That value is an asterisk, the same character Linux uses in /etc/shadow to mark an account as having no password. OpenSSH then treats the returned asterisk as a match and permits the login.
The conditions to exploit the vulnerability are however quite narrow. The server must run OpenSSH before version 10.6p2, be built against the musl library rather than glibc, and operate without PAM. It must also have at least one account with a SHA-256 or SHA-512 password hash and another account marked with an asterisk in its shadow entry. When those conditions are met, any password between 257 and 1,024 characters can authenticate against the passwordless account.
Alpine Linux is the most prominent distribution affected, as it uses musl and its default OpenSSH configuration does not enable PAM. Other musl-based environments, including OpenWrt, Buildroot and Yocto, may also be affected where the same configuration applies. Systems using glibc, PAM, …

California sues OpenAI over rogue AI hacking incidents
OpenAI lost control of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing, California’s AG claims.
The lawsuit claims the cyberattack on Hugging Face “was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability.” It alleges that OpenAI recently told the attorney general’s office that it “lost control” of its AI agents more than 80 times during testing.

Uno Platform is an open-source framework for building .NET applications with C# and WinUI XAML for Windows, Android, iOS, macOS, Linux and WebAssembly. The team describes 7.0 as its largest release, with 5,219 commits and 704 closed issues since 6.7. According to the team’s benchmarks, 7.0 is about 2x faster at the median and 5x smaller than 6.7, with some operations, such as brush creation, up to 38x faster. These figures come from the vendor and the workloads were not published in detail.
All targets now render through one pluggable pipeline. SkiaSharp 4 is the default, and Uno Platform is a co-maintainer of the library alongside the .NET team at Microsoft. articles.summary:
The Artex agentic AI penetration testing framework has become a common tool in Chinese threat actors’ arsenal, and Barracuda is one of its victims.
Published on GitHub in July 2026, Artex relies on a planner to formulate an objective and create tasks based on it, and on agents to perform those tasks, while the platform itself records the progress, findings, and assets.
It reportedly used DeepSeek v4.1-flash as the initial model, but can use other LLMs as well, and GLM-5.3 and Grok 4.6 were observed in certain instances. Overall, however, its users mainly rely on Chinese models, which are more permissive compared to US-made ones.
Artex was designed for security testing, but threat actors have been using it as part of in-the-wild intrusions since at least August, and its occurrence in real-world attacks has increased significantly during the past several weeks.
“The framework enables threat actors with minimal technical expertise to conduct complex, multi-target operations simultaneously, fundamentally accelerating attack velocity and expanding operational scale,” the FBI warns in a new alert (PDF).
Mentioning the framework’s use in attacks on South Korean financial firms and ConnectWise, the FBI warns of the risks Artex poses: faster attacks through automation, exploitation of neglected peripheral devices, and the ability to find and exploit supply chain attack vectors.

articles.title: 7 Tips For Complying with CJIS Password and MFA Requirements
articles.summary:
Compromised passwords and gaps in multi-factor authentication (MFA) remain common ways attackers gain access to sensitive systems. For law enforcement agencies handling criminal justice information (CJI), protecting against these threats is also a matter of CJIS compliance.
The FBI's latest CJIS Security Policy sets clear requirements for password management and MFA. these are Priority 1 (P1) controls, so must be implemented immediately to comply. But this can be challenging, particularly across the complex IT environments that are common in law enforcement.
This guide contains practical tips to help agencies meet the latest requirements, strengthen their defenses against credential-based attacks, and make ongoing compliance easier to manage.
1. Enforce Stronger Minimum Password Lengths
CJIS requires user-selected passwords to be at least eight characters long, or six characters if generated by a credential service provider or verifier using an approved random number generator. However, we recommend going beyond these minimums and encouraging passphrases of at least 15 characters.
Longer passwords are generally harder to crack, and passphrases can be easier to remember than shorter passwords with complex combinations of symbols and numbers.
CJIS doesn't require traditional complexity rules, so focus on length and strength rather than arbitrary character requirements.

articles.title: Usable Security at Luxury Hotels - Schneier on Security

Usable Security at Luxury Hotels
Interesting case study from luxury hotels. Attackers used a fake booking request to gain access to a reservations inbox, where they copied genuine refund requests and got fraudulent ones approved.
This is a good illustration why “just don’t click on links” is bad advice. It can’t work when answering strangers’ emails is the job. Even worse, in this case the guest-first culture punishes hesitation. More interesting, the case study shows that splitting security between owner, operator, and brand leaves nobody accountable. And this is exactly the setting where blaming staff becomes the convenient answer.
TimH • November 16, 2026 7:22 AM
TFA: “We suspect a colleague opened the email and clicked the link, unknowingly giving the attackers access to the reservations shared inbox.”
So there was no front-end layer checking inbox content for such dubiosities? Or limiting access to specific computer MACs, or intranet IP ranges.
The ball is in the IT org’s court for not setting this up.
Same with IT who can’t set a limit of 5 CCs on emails to stop an email blast CCing every customer.

Nigeria now has rules that officially recognise stablecoins as payment and settlement instruments, giving issuers a framework to distribute tokens backed by fiat currencies. The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) divides these tokens into two: naira-referenced and foreign currency-referenced stablecoins.
Stablecoins are digital currencies designed to maintain the value of currencies such as the naira or US dollar. Companies issuing them must hold enough money and other assets to back the tokens in circulation—which they create.
Under the new rules, foreign currency-backed issuers must hold up to ₦15 billion ($11.16 million) in minimum capital, while naira-backed issuers must hold ₦10 billion ($7.44 million). But the more consequential requirements concern what happens to customers’ money after they buy stablecoins.
Stablecoin holders cannot earn interest on their tokens, even though issuers can invest the money backing those tokens in interest-bearing assets. Cryptocurrency exchanges and other virtual asset service providers (VASPs) distributing regulated stablecoins cannot offer yield on behalf of issuers either.

articles.title: Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
articles.summary:
Sponsored
Building trustworthy AI by fencing it in, not predicting it
While we’re used to predictable technology, AI challenges that assumption. Therefore, the goal must be bounded, observable, and controllable AI.
Provided byUL Solutions
In October this year, OpenAI disclosed that two of its AI agents had switched off the systems built to monitor them. One muted its own safety alerts after misreading an instruction not to send messages; the other removed its monitoring integration during migration, then said it hadn’t. No rule had told the agents to do that, and no test had anticipated the behaviors.
For a century, we have built trust in technology on predictability: predefined inputs, predictable outputs, and layers of protection. Consider how a breaker trips at a set current or an aircraft component is tested against known (i.e., predictable) stresses.
AI changes that. Traditional software executes instructions written by humans, whereas AI exercises what might be called synthetic judgment. We use AI because it can interpret situations we did not program and generate responses we did not prescribe. But the more freedom we give AI, the harder it becomes to provide the predictability on which trust has traditionally been built.

articles.title: GitHub Rebuilds the Copilot App's Diff Surface to Open Million-Line Pull Requests Without Jank
articles.summary:
GitHub engineering has published a detailed account of how it rebuilt the diff surface in the GitHub Copilot app to open a pull request with 2,200 files, over a million changed lines and more than 400 inline review comments without turning the review into a waiting exercise.
The post, by Principal Design Engineer Alberto Gimeno, lands at a moment when AI coding agents are producing far more pull requests than reviewers can digest, and the bottleneck has moved from writing code to reading it.
At the heart of the rebuild is a decision to stop pretending a pull request is a single uniform list. Code rows have a known height at a known font size, so their geometry can be computed up front and never rebuilt. Comments do not. A markdown body wraps differently at different widths, <details> sections can be toggled in place, reply composers grow as a user types, and images change height when they load. Rather than force one variable-height virtualizer to absorb both, the team split the document into two independent domains:
total height = deterministic code height
 + Σ dynamic block effective heights

articles.title: Delivery drones are coming. For some with PTSD, that's a terrifying prospect.

In August, Amazon announced plans to expand its Prime Air delivery drone program to “nearly 500 cities and towns by the end of 2026.” Combined with similar uncrewed aerial delivery programs from DoorDash and Zipline (in partnership with Uber and Walmart), the expansion suggests that flying robots dropping their payloads onto suburban lawns will soon be commonplace.
For many people, delivery drones will be little more than a novelty, occasionally good for a laugh when one does something ridiculous. For others, though, their growing use could be a nightmare. As the instant delivery industry clears the last FAA hurdles to rapid deliveries beyond an operator’s line of sight, an increasing number of people worldwide are living with post-traumatic stress disorder or other anxiety-related disorders triggered by drones.
The use of all manner of weaponized drones in the ongoing war in Ukraine and in Israeli attacks on Lebanon and Gaza has already produced an epidemic of what some mental health professionals have dubbed “dronophobia.” And while relatively few US troops have been targeted by drones flown by Iran, ISIS, and Iran-backed militias throughout the Middle East, even those who have not directly been attacked may experience anxiety simply because of the ample video footage of attacks circulating in news and social media.

articles.title: Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing | Amazon Web Services

Artificial Intelligence
Taxonomy of multi-agent design patterns, anti-patterns, and lessons from manufacturing
Enterprise teams are building multi-agent systems, and when early implementations fall short, the cause is rarely the model. Multi-agent coordination is a distributed systems problem, and many teams taking it on haven’t yet built distributed systems instincts.
The numbers are consistent across sources: ~88% of AI pilots never reach production. Stanford HAI demonstrated that two models can perform worse collaborating than either alone when coordination overhead exceeds the benefit. The pattern is clear: teams are adding complexity faster than they build understanding. Ten steps that are each 95 percent reliable deliver only 59.9 percent end-to-end reliability, and 20 steps deliver 35.8 percent. This illustrative model assumes a strictly sequential chain with no retries, but the direction holds: each dependent handoff multiplies risk.
In this post, you learn how to decide whether a use case needs multiple agents, choose a coordination pattern, and spot costly anti-patterns early. You also see how takt time, safety boundaries, edge data, and shift cycles shape the architecture.
Multi-agent coordination patterns
Coordination patterns fall into two tiers, based on who controls the flow. In Tier 1, you define the path.
In Tier 2, the model chooses the path at runtime. That flexibility handles work whose steps you can’t define in advance, at a higher cost in tokens, latency…

What we know so far: The nationwide ground stop that froze US air travel on Friday didn't start at a major hub or a busy control center. It began at a small FAA radio site in El Dorado, Arkansas, where a router installed during routine upgrade work began flooding the agency's private network with connection requests that the older equipment it connected to couldn't handle. Soon after, the links between pilots and controllers and the radar feeds that track aircraft started failing.
The result was more than 3,500 flights held for about five hours, leaving tens of thousands of travelers stranded.
The volume of traffic was far beyond anything the network normally handles. "We saw two places that were actually pinging our network at a very high rate, a thousand connections over every four to five seconds," Rebecca Guy, the FAA's technology chief, said on Saturday at a press conference.
El Dorado was one of those two places. The other was a radar facility in Amarillo, Texas, which had been upgraded several weeks earlier and showed a second problem that officials have not described. Engineers took both sites offline, but by then each had been hitting the network hundreds of times per second. That was enough to knock out other parts of the air traffic communications system, and the delays and cancellations carried into the weekend.

C’est normal, puisque la distance est bien plus courte : environ 590 à 630 kilomètres d’altitude pour les satellites d’Amazon, contre 35 000 km environ pour les satellites géostationnaires.
