Anders als Pangram und weitere KI-Dektoren: Kann man erkennen, ob eine Idee von ChatGPT stammt?
Schulen, Hochschulen, Wissenschaft und Medien, sie alle befinden sich in einem Katz-und-Maus-Spiel mit künstlicher Intelligenz: Welche Hausaufgaben, Studien und Berichte stammen von einem Menschen und welche wurden von einem großen Sprachmodell verfasst? Wo wurde KI als Hilfsmittel verwendet, um Texte zu formulieren und wo war sie womöglich stärker involviert, vielleicht sogar beim Erstellen von Daten oder gar der Ideenfindung?

In context: Back when tweets were capped at 140 characters, brands and politicians ran most of their links through Bitly to shrink them down. That's why years of old posts on X are still full of tiny bit.ly addresses. Click one, and the service quietly forwards you to the full web page sitting behind it. Most people wouldn't think twice before doing that. Over the weekend, pranksters managed to take over some of those old links in posts from Donald Trump, McDonald's and Burger King.
CNN found that Trump's account was hit the hardest. At least a dozen of his posts now carry swapped links, including a 2013 complaint about wind turbines. Open it today, and you'll land on a Google site called "fortnite baby," complete with a photo of an infant.
Over at Burger King, a 2011 post meant to help people find nearby restaurants now leads to Wikipedia's list of Nazi concentration camps. McDonald's didn't escape either – one of its 2011 posts now opens a page about the September 11 attacks.
Bill Gates, former Canadian prime minister Justin Trudeau and Mike Pence all had old posts tampered with as well. Weirdly, the FBI's 2012 post about its "Ghost Clicks" case now just shows a photo of a seal.
In theory, none of this should be possible. Bitly's own help pages say the code at the end of a short link can never be reused, even after the account that created it gets deleted.

Qué ha ocurrido. Tres días antes, el consejo había abierto una investigación porque Huang había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia extranjera, y había dicho que confiaba en él. Entre líneas. El analista Gene Munster ha subido del 10% al 51% las probabilidades de que Huang vuelva. Su argumento es que el consejo le forzó a dimitir, y que esa forma de salir permite que la readmisión sea más sencilla, ya que no implica una admisión de que el consejo se equivocó.
Si en 72 horas pasó de “confiamos en Jensen” a enseñarle la puerta de salida, la tortilla puede volver a girar igual de rápido.
Sí, pero. La palabra elegida cuenta poco:
- Steve Jobs también dimitió, en 1985, después de que le quitaran todas sus funciones. Volvió doce años después, cuando Apple, al borde de la quiebra, compró NeXT.

Lo que decide estos casos es quién puede presionar al consejo.

The demo's 3D space and textures are all procedurally generated, meaning they're the result of mathematical equations rather than prebuilt 3D meshes, and all calculated on load. Using actual meshes and images for textures would otherwise take up a significant amount of space.

Teams point the AWS CLI or an AWS SDK at it with environment variables such as AWS_ENDPOINT_URL, leaving application code unchanged. Rust tests can use an embedded mode that runs the emulator inside the test process and wires its HTTP client into the AWS SDK for Rust. An aws-emulator skill can start the emulator for coding agents and check a project against published fidelity tests. AWS says agents wrote and tested the code. Matthew Goldberg, a senior principal engineer at AWS, describes three teams: one writes fidelity tests from the public API models and verifies them against real AWS, one replays those tests and files issues, and one implements each fix. Lo que dice el artículo 21. El precepto regula el impago de los gastos comunes, las medidas que puede pactar la comunidad, la reclamación judicial y la mediación o el arbitraje, y buena parte de ese contenido se incorporó con la Ley 10/2022. Y es que fue esa reforma la que permitió a la junta aprobar medidas disuasorias contra los morosos, siempre que no sean abusivas ni afecten a la habitabilidad.
La obligación de pagar está en el artículo 9.1.e de la Ley de Propiedad Horizontal, y para reclamar lo que se debe la comunidad puede tirar del proceso monitorio especial, sin que el artículo 21 fije un importe máximo.

Pues que, según el artículo 15.2, quien no esté al corriente de sus deudas al empezar la reunión puede participar en las deliberaciones, pero no votar, salvo que las haya impugnado judicialmente o haya consignado lo que debe. El resultado fue SMART, un sistema que prometía reducir demoras y cancelaciones, y que en cuestión de semanas pasó de proyecto piloto a herramienta nacional. Lo que nadie anticipaba era que su estreno a escala plena coincidiría con el peor colapso aéreo de Estados Unidos en casi cuatro años.
El viernes 13 de noviembre, la FAA ordenó la paralización total del espacio aéreo a las 3:54 p.m. hora del este.
El ground stop duró más de cuatro horas y dejó un saldo de más de 5.000 vuelos cancelados y al menos 827 desviados antes de las 7:05 p.m., según datos de Cirium citados por AP.
Qué es SMART y por qué quedó en el centro de la escena
El 10 de noviembre, la FAA extendió SMART (Strategic Management of Airspace, Routes and Trajectories) a los 22 centros de control de tráfico aéreo del país. Hasta ese momento, el sistema solo operaba como prueba piloto en la región de Washington D.C. desde septiembre.
SMART es una plataforma en la nube que analiza horarios de vuelo, condiciones climáticas, capacidad aeroportuaria y personal de control para anticipar congestionamientos y sugerir rutas más eficientes.

Apple veut en finir avec Touch ID sur son smartphone pliant et préparer le retour de Face ID. Mais alors que les ingénieurs travaillent activement sur son intégration à l’écran extérieur de l’iPhone Duo 2, rien ne garantit que cette nouveauté sera prête à temps.
Attendu à l’automne prochain, l’iPhone Duo 2 pourrait ne pas se contenter d’améliorations classiques au niveau de la puce et des appareils photo. D’après Mark Gurman, journaliste chez Bloomberg, Apple aurait notamment deux objectifs pour cette nouvelle génération : intégrer Face ID et ajouter un bouton Action.
Face ID devient la priorité du prochain iPhone Duo
La présence de Touch ID en lieu et place de Face ID demeure sans nul doute parmi les aspects les plus dommageables du premier pliant d’Apple. Pour la prochaine génération d’iPhone Duo, la marque à la pomme plancherait justement à améliorer le système de reconnaissance faciale. Les équipes d’Apple auraient déjà mis au point plusieurs prototypes du smartphone avec cette technologie, et poursuivraient actuellement leurs travaux pour la faire fonctionner à travers l’écran extérieur.
Mark Gurman indique cependant que les délais sont serrés et que la fonctionnalité n’est pas encore prête. Il ne confirme donc pas sa présence sur le modèle qui doit être commercialisé l’année prochaine. Malgré son statut de priorité pour Apple, Face ID pourrait ainsi manquer le lancement de l’iPhone Duo 2.
Un bouton Action et d’autres évolutions à l’étude

articles.title: James Bond : quel sera le smartphone de Robert Pattinson ? Retour sur 30 ans d'évolution à travers les films — Frandroid
articles.summary:
Amazon MGM Studios a annoncé ce lundi 16 novembre que Robert Pattinson reprendra le rôle de James Bond, dans un film réalisé par Denis Villeneuve sur un scénario de Steven Knight. Fin de plusieurs années de rumeurs.
Chez Frandroid, une autre question nous travaille : quel smartphone aura-t-il dans la poche ? La question n’est pas si futile. Depuis la fin des années 90, le mobile de 007 est l’un des placements produits les plus convoités du cinéma. Quand on remet les modèles bout à bout, on obtient une petite histoire de l’industrie mobile : Ericsson, puis Sony Ericsson, puis Sony seul, puis la renaissance (éphémère) de Nokia.
1997, l’Ericsson JB988 : le dernier vrai téléphone de Q
Le premier téléphone vraiment marquant de Bond n’a jamais été vendu. Dans Demain ne meurt jamais (1997), Pierce Brosnan dégaine un Ericsson JB988, un modèle fictif conçu spécialement pour le film, sans équivalent dans le catalogue de la marque.
C’est un pur gadget de Q. Il cache un crochet de serrure dans l’antenne, un lecteur d’empreintes digitales et une décharge de 20 000 volts. Surtout, il se déplie pour révéler un pavé tactile qui permet à James Bond de piloter sa BMW 750iL depuis la banquette arrière, une caméra embarquée en guise de rétroviseur.
Mine de rien, le JB988 a eu du flair. Le lecteur d’empreintes est devenu banal sur nos smartphones, et le JB988 l’imaginait seize ans avant le Touch ID de l’iPhone, lancé en 2013. En outre, démarrer, déverrouiller ou déplacer sa voiture depuis son tél…

articles.title: Ookla report finds that some Asian cities have 50 times better indoor mobile signal than US and UK ones — and no, it’s not because of building materials
articles.summary:
Ookla report reveals why your indoor mobile signal is so bad — cities in North America and UK top global rankings for buildings with 4G signal below 105 dBm
Bad outdoors, worse indoors
- Ookla has found that North America, Europe, and Oceania have worse indoor mobile signal than other regions
- The difference in signal power can be up to around 50 times
- This is primarily down to these regions having poor outdoor signal in cities too
If you live in North America or Europe then you’ve probably frequently found that your phone’s signal is bad indoors — but the main reason might not be what you’d assume.
Ookla has carried out a study, comparing indoor and outdoor signal measurements across over 100 cities globally, and it has found that indoor signal is weakest in North America, Europe, and Oceania.
But if you assumed the problem was building materials, well, you’d be — mostly — wrong. According to Ookla, the material a building is constructed from can make a difference to a signal’s ability to pass through walls, but it’s not a dramatic difference, with timber-framed buildings reducing a signal by 2 dB (decibels), while concrete ones still only drop it by 7 dB, with the median drop being 4 dB.
That accounts for under a tenth of the overall difference in indoor signal between different cities and regions, with 85% of the difference coming from how good the outdoor signal is. So in other words, cities with better outdoor signal tend to have better indoor signal, too — which isn'…

articles.title: FBI says Artex AI open source hacking tool used to breach networks in 'under three hours' | TechCrunch
articles.summary:
The FBI is warning that hackers are relying on autonomous AI hacking tools to launch cyberattacks across the U.S. and globally. The campaigns include a widespread hack of customers of American IT company ConnectWise and across South Korea’s financial industry.
In its latest flash cybersecurity advisory, the FBI says hackers have targeted several industries in recent months, including financial services, government, tech, defense, phone and internet companies, and law firms, using open source tools like Artex to carry out autonomous-driven cyberattacks.
Artex is one of several open source AI-powered penetration testing platforms, a category of software built to probe a network’s defenses. Hackers can connect Artex to hosted frontier large language models (LLMs) like those from Anthropic and OpenAI, as well as to open source models and non-U.S. models. The FBI says Artex intrusions can be “noisy,” meaning they generate reams of traffic and data that may trigger a targeted company’s defensive alerts. But the tools allow hackers to move at speeds that make it far more difficult for human defenders to keep up.
In some cases, Artex-linked attacks can move from targeting a system to active compromise “in under three hours.”
The FBI’s warning comes as AI-powered hacks are escalating, particularly by finding easy-to-find security flaws and breaking into companies with relative ease.
Oftentimes, Artex will rely on rapidly scanning a victim’s network to look for signs of weakness, and t…

articles.title: US now "comfortable" with children dying of measles as death toll hits 10
articles.summary:
Health officials in Pennsylvania and Wisconsin announced two more measles deaths late last week, bringing the national tally of confirmed measles deaths this year to 10. The total includes the deaths of at least four infants: two in Pennsylvania, one in New York, and one in Wisconsin.
Wisconsin health officials said the latest measles death—the second for the state—was in a child. Pennsylvania’s health department did not reveal the age or other details of the latest death—the state’s seventh—besides revealing it was of an unvaccinated resident in Montour County. Overall, the seven deaths in Pennsylvania include two in Jefferson County, three in Lancaster County, and one in Mifflin, in addition to the new death in Montour. An eighth death was reported in Franklin County, but state health officials have not confirmed it.
For all the states with deaths so far, health officials have noted that they’re the first deaths in decades. Multiple outbreaks are underway across the country, pushing the national tally of cases to nearly 5,500 across 47 states and jurisdictions, according to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Pennsylvania’s case count alone is over 1,500, and Wisconsin is reporting nearly 650.
Lost status

articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage led to chlorine gas leak at German hotel, poisoning of 15 guests and sending four to hospital
articles.summary:
WTF?! The recent global outage of Microsoft 365 services affected millions across the world, but the impact on people varied enormously. Take, for example, the 15 guests at a hotel in Germany who were exposed to a chlorine gas leak as a result of the debacle. That sounds a lot worse than not being able to use Teams.
According to regional publication WDR (via Notebookcheck), the incident happened at the Hotel Ling Bao, part of Phantasialand theme park in Germany. It experienced a malfunction with its dosing system, which pumped too much chlorine into the pool.
The facility uses a maintenance safety system in its sauna area that sends emails warning when chlorine levels are too high. But because of the Microsoft 365 service disruption, the emails never arrived.
Forty first responders were dispatched to the incident. Fifteen people required triage due to respiratory irritation, four were taken to the hospital, and one had to remain under observation due to an injury.
The disruption began on November 12, when users around the world started reporting problems with Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Teams, and Copilot. Downdetector received nearly 150,000 complaints, while Microsoft said its servers were experiencing unusually heavy loads. Outlook users couldn't send emails or access their inboxes, and some servers went offline again after being restored.

Falha no dosador elevou o nível de cloro na piscina de um hotel na Alemanha. Alerta enviado por e-mail não chegou aos funcionários durante a pane do Outlook.
Quinze pessoas foram afetadas por uma exposição a níveis elevados de cloro na piscina de um hotel na Alemanha. O incidente ocorreu durante a pane global que deixou Outlook e outros serviços da Microsoft instáveis. A interrupção impediu que um alerta automático sobre o problema chegasse aos funcionários do estabelecimento.
O caso aconteceu no Hotel Ling Bao, que faz parte do parque temático Phantasialand, na cidade de Brühl. Segundo a emissora alemã WDR, uma falha no sistema automático de dosagem fez com que uma quantidade excessiva de cloro fosse despejada na piscina.
O sistema de segurança responsável por monitorar a manutenção da área detectou o problema e enviou um aviso por e-mail aos funcionários. Como o Outlook e o Exchange Online estavam fora do ar, a mensagem não foi entregue. A equipe só percebeu que havia algo errado depois que pessoas na piscina começaram a apresentar problemas respiratórios.
Equipes de emergência e bombeiros foram acionados para atender as vítimas. Ao todo, 15 pessoas passaram por avaliação médica, a maioria com irritação nas vias respiratórias. Quatro foram levadas ao hospital, e uma delas permaneceu internada em observação por causa de ferimentos considerados moderados.

articles.title: Un arquitecto técnico experto en ahorro energético lo explica: "A una bomba de calor le va bien que le pidas poco, que sea una casa, que esté bien aislada"
articles.summary:
Cambiar la caldera de gas por una bomba de calor parece la manera más rápida de pagar menos por la calefacción, pero puedes encontrarte con que apenas hay diferencia. Por eso, el arquitecto técnico Jordi Martí avisa en su canal de TikTok de que el aparato no garantiza por sí solo una factura mucho más baja, y lo ilustra de una forma bastante gráfica: “A una bomba de calor le va bien que le pidas poco, que sea una casa, que esté bien aislada”.
Lo que pide la bomba de calor. Las bombas de calor rinden mejor y ahorran más cuando no necesitan ir siempre al límite, que es cuando tu vivienda está bien aislada y conserva bien la temperatura. Por eso, se puede decir que el ahorro depende tanto del aparato como de la construcción de la vivienda, el sistema de calefacción que tiene e incluso tus ventanas. La OCU también apunta en esta dirección en su guía para preparar la casa, donde recuerda que el nivel de aislamiento influye en la eficiencia de la bomba de calor, y por eso simplemente cambiar la caldera dejando lo demás igual no es siempre suficiente.
La teoría y la factura. “En teoría debería dividir el consumo por tres o por cuatro, pero miras las facturas y eso no lo notas tanto. Y el confort, pues eso, que a veces no da”, señala el arquitecto. Eso sí, según Martí, si la casa tiene poco aislamiento, ventanas antiguas o muchas pérdidas, el aparato tiene que trabajar bastante más tiempo, y si los radiadores exigen temperaturas elevadas, la bomba pierde ventaja.

articles.title: Jensen Huang: The anatomy of a scandal
articles.summary:
Prevention is better than cure. We know the public relations (PR) adage. But it would be glib to leave it hanging when faced with a doom-laden news cycle like Nvidia’s. The question is how a scandal of this scale takes hold, how far the fallout spreads, and what it takes to rebuild trust when the damage extends well beyond the individual at its centre—as of Friday, November 13, $493 billion had reportedly been wiped off Nvidia’s value.
They say ‘sex sells’, but it also costs. The unfolding scandal surrounding Jensen Huang, Nvidia’s former CEO, is a case in point. What began as reporting about an alleged relationship with a woman US intelligence officials believe was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security has spiralled into a much bigger story involving personal relationships, workplace power dynamics, corporate governance, national security, shareholder confidence, and an enthusiastic internet meme culture.
This is no longer simply a story about a billionaire’s personal life. There is gossip, and then there is national security. It has become a case study in what happens when personal conduct, corporate reputation, and geopolitical interests collide. For African tech founders, this risk is familiar. When the founder is the person investors back and the ecosystem trusts, their personal conduct can quickly become everybody’s business.

articles.title: California sues OpenAI over AI agents escaping sandboxes, hacking firms
articles.summary:
California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI on Monday, alleging the company knowingly continued testing advanced artificial intelligence models despite repeated security failures that allowed autonomous AI agents to escape isolated environments and launch cyberattacks against real-world organizations.
The lawsuit claims OpenAI misled the public about its cybersecurity safeguards and failed to adequately monitor increasingly advanced AI cybersecurity models, resulting in more than 80 incidents in which the company lost control of its agents during testing.
The legal action follows a July security incident where hundreds of OpenAI-powered agents escaped a controlled testing environment and hacked Hugging Face, an artificial intelligence platform, compromising production infrastructure and stealing internal credentials.
California says the Hugging Face attack resulted from OpenAI repeatedly focusing on experimental AI testing without ensuring adequate safeguards were in place.
"The Hugging Face cyberattack was the predictable result of an internal culture at OpenAI that prioritizes growth and rapid model development over safety and accountability," the complaint reads.
The lawsuit alleges that OpenAI continued testing increasingly capable AI agents despite knowing its sandbox environments could be bypassed, potentially exposing third-party systems to unauthorized activity.

Qué se necesita para duplicar la pantalla del celular en el TV
El requisito principal es que ambos dispositivos estén conectados a la misma red WiFi. Si el teléfono utiliza una red distinta de la que tiene configurada el Smart TV, no podrá detectar la TV ni enviar la imagen. Hace falta encender el televisor y comprobar que sus opciones de conexión inalámbrica estén activadas.
Asimismo, la estabilidad de la red influye en el resultado. Una conexión de 5 GHz puede reducir las demoras al reproducir videos o compartir imágenes de alta resolución.
Cuando hay muchos dispositivos conectados al mismo WiFi, la transmisión puede sufrir cortes, pérdida de fluidez o un retraso entre lo que ocurre en el teléfono y lo que aparece en el TV.

articles.title: Governed Autonomous Intelligence for Mission-Critical Utility
articles.summary:
Key Takeaways
- In a regulated utility environment, an agentic operations platform keeps reasoning separate from execution: agents correlate signals, assess business impact, and propose remediation, but every production action crosses a deterministic policy boundary that the model cannot override.
- That boundary is defined outside the model. Each proposed action maps to a risk class and approval requirement in a predefined, versioned action catalog, which keeps approval decisions predictable, testable, and reviewable before deployment.
- A governed tool gateway enforces the boundary as the only path from an agent proposal to a production change, with least privilege, independent authorization, approval verification, and complete action evidence attached to that single door.
- Because every action passes through one governed path, the platform produces the evidence needed to support the regulatory and governance requirements of each system, without claiming that the platform itself creates compliance.
- Autonomy is earned rather than assumed: the platform starts read-only and expands one action class at a time, guided by recommendation quality, operator acceptance, execution outcomes, and rollback safety, and that autonomy can be revoked as easily as it is granted.

India's fintech decade was built on distribution. The next one will be built on infrastructure, advice and intelligence—and capital is already repricing accordingly.
India spent the last ten years solving for reach. UPI, Aadhaar-based onboarding, and the Jan Dhan push put a payment instrument in almost every adult hand, and a generation of companies was built on that distribution. That problem is now largely solved. The harder question—how to serve those hundreds of millions of customers profitably, with products that measurably improve their financial lives—is where the next cycle of venture capital will go.
The funding data already reflects the shift. Indian fintech attracted $3.5 billion across 216 disclosed deals in 2024, and $2.9 billion across 156 deals in 2025 roughly 10% less capital across 27% fewer transactions, according to Fintech Global. This fits fewer, larger cheques into a narrower set of theses. Yet fintech remained the largest sector by funding in 2025 at 22% of all Indian startup capital, and close to 26% in the first half of 2026. Capital is not leaving the sector; it is becoming far more selective about where to park itself.
Three themes stand out as most likely to absorb that capital over the next 24 months.

Microsoft informou que o "apagão" recente no Outlook e em outros serviços foi causado por uma falha em uma atualização de software aplicada em julho.
O “apagão” que a Microsoft sofreu na última semana, que manteve o Outlook e vários serviços da companhia inacessíveis ou instáveis por horas, deixou algumas dúvidas no ar, entre elas, “a companhia teria sido alvo de hackers?”. Bom, de acordo com a própria empresa, o problema foi causado por falha em uma atualização de software.
Chega a ser irônico, pois atualizações de software visam corrigir falhas, não causá-las. Mas foi o que aconteceu aqui. Em um relatório preliminar sobre o caso, a companhia explica que o problema começou em uma atualização aplicada em julho deste ano em servidores de “gateway de rede” ligados ao Microsoft 365.
Esses servidores controlam o acesso aos serviços da empresa (embora não respondam pela autenticação de usuários), recebendo solicitações dos usuários e as encaminhando para os sistemas que devem lidar com elas. Se essa dinâmica falha, os tais serviços deixam de ser acessados.
A tal atualização de software visava corrigir um problema anterior. Depois que o procedimento foi realizado, nenhuma anormalidade foi percebida. Testes de carga de trabalho chegaram a ser executados, mas nenhum deles apontou falhas ou sinais de impactos operacionais negativos. Mas o problema estava lá.

articles.title: Airbnb Introduces CASTLE for Training Natural Language Search Models with Synthetic Data
articles.summary:
Airbnb researchers have introduced CASTLE, a framework designed to address the cold-start problem in natural language search. The approach uses de-identified booking sessions and large language models (LLMs) to jointly generate synthetic search queries and relevance labels, enabling model training before sufficient real search traffic is available.
Natural language search allows guests to describe their preferences in everyday language, such as "romantic cabin near skiing" or "pet-friendly beach house that sleeps eight", rather than relying exclusively on predefined filters. Training such systems presents two challenges: generating queries that reflect actual user behavior and determining which property listings are relevant to each query.
Previous approaches, including InPars and Promptagator, address query generation and relevance labeling as separate tasks. They use LLMs to generate queries from documents or examples, followed by additional model-based judgments to assign relevance labels. According to the researchers, this separation can introduce additional sources of error and differences between synthetic and real-user query distributions.
CASTLE uses contrastive listing pairs derived from de-identified booking sessions. When a guest books a property after viewing several alternatives, the selected listing becomes a positive example, while another viewed but unbooked property serves as a negative example. An LLM is then prompted to generate a query that matches the pos…

articles.title: Google Project Zero cuts bug disclosures to 30 days amid AI threats
articles.summary:
Google Project Zero will replace its “90+30” disclosure policy with shorter, fixed deadlines in response to AI-accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation.
The transition is gradual and began on November 13, when the 30-day extension was removed from the vulnerability disclosure timeline.
On February 2, 2027, the deadline will be further reduced to 60 days, and on January 3, 2028, it will shrink to just 30 days.
Once the deadline expires, Project Zero will publish vulnerability details even if a fix is not available.
Project Zero is Google’s vulnerability research team, focused on the discovery of serious security flaws in widely used software and hardware.
Some of its notable recent findings include a .NET Framework zero-day, flaws in Chrome’s JavaScript engine and graphics components, and a Qualcomm chipset zero-day linked to NoviSpy spyware attacks.
When the team finds a flaw, it reports it privately to the vendor and typically publishes the technical details after a set period, giving time for developing security updates and patches, as well as a margin for most users to apply them.
Project Zero says AI has accelerated vulnerability discovery and exploitation, and made it easier for attackers to reverse-engineer fixes as soon as patches ship and develop working exploits.
This policy change puts greater pressure on vendors to investigate reports, develop fixes, and ship them faster to customers.

Started with a founder’s college fees, oho Living survived its worst year and now runs 1,032 beds across six Tier-2 cities.
Anyone who has moved to a new city for college or a first job knows the feeling. You arrive with a suitcase and an address you can barely find, and the room you are handed is bare. Nobody tells you where to buy groceries or whom to call when the geyser breaks. You figure it out alone.
In cities like Ranchi, Patna and Jaipur, the choice was usually between expensive premium housing and bare rooms with no standard at all. Students and young professionals who wanted a clean, well-run home at a fair price had nowhere to go, and landlords and young tenants rarely trusted each other.
oho Living was built to fill that gap. It now runs 1,032 beds across six cities, with one promise: to be the friend in the city for everyone who moves to one.
From listings to homes
Ritu Raj had tried to solve this once before. In college, he built GoForRooms, a website that helped students find a place to stay. It could point someone to a room, but it could not promise what living there would be like.
So when he started oho Living, paying for it with his college fees, the team chose to run the homes themselves. It began with a single property in Ranchi, run the way a friend would run it, and grew one property and one city at a time.

articles.title: Cyber criminals are shopping for victims with Black Friday scams according to new Norton research - Tech Guide

Black Friday is quickly approaching and while you’re shopping for bargains, cyber criminals are looking for victims after new research from Norton showed a 155 per cent surge in blocked fake online store attacks.
In Australia, more than 2.25 million attacks were blocked during last year’s shopping period between October and December 2025.
The latest 2026 Norton Insights report: Holiday Scams shows that 13 per cent of Australians have fallen victim to a holiday shopping scam.
And 94 per cent of those victims lost money.
On average victims lost $1,327 but the highest reported loss was around $30,000.
The research has also highlighted some emerging risks including AI shopping assistants used by 57 per cent of Australians that recommend or completed a purchase from an unfamiliar retailer during the most recent holiday shopping season.
Only 46 per cent of Australians are confident an AI shopping assistant would be able to recognise and avoid a fraudulent website.
Alarmingly 27 per cent have admitted purchasing from a seller they suspected might have been a scam because the deal was too good to miss.
Social media is also playing its part, with 42 per cent of holiday shopping scam victims admitting they were scammed through these platforms.
Of those shopping for trending gifts like Labubu or Jellycat, 36 per cent encountered suspicious websites or sellers.

articles.summary:
The stunning return of Starship from the skies to a launch tower in South Texas answered some questions about the future of SpaceX’s ambitious rocket program. Namely, it is now rapidly moving toward rapidly reusable launch.
However, it raises other questions. For example, as Starship becomes fully reusable, when might humans fly on the vehicle?
The short answer is pretty simple: If SpaceX prioritizes human spaceflight on Starship, it could happen reasonably quickly. The longer answer becomes more complicated and depends on what one means by human spaceflight. The first people to fly on Starship probably won’t launch from Earth, or land here. Rather, they will probably be NASA’s lunar astronauts. So there are different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth.
Given what is known publicly, and what Ars has heard privately, here are some educated guesses about all of this.
Past is prologue
The first thing we can say for sure is that all estimates of human spaceflight on Starship should be taken with a gigantic grain of salt, including those in this article. Putting humans on any space vehicle is a difficult and time-consuming task, even outside of the requirements that NASA would impose for its astronauts.

articles.title: Microsoft adds a way to remotely lock lost Windows 11 laptops without wiping them
articles.summary:
In context: Windows 11 allows IT administrators to remotely wipe corporate laptops that have been lost or stolen using Microsoft's Intune device management software. Microsoft is now experimenting with a new Remote Locking option designed to protect sensitive data from unauthorized access without deleting any files.
As explained on Microsoft's Learn website, Remote Lock offers a less destructive way to protect data on lost or stolen devices than Remote Wipe. While Remote Wipe deletes all user data from a device, the new feature leaves the data untouched. If the device is recovered, its authorized user can simply sign in and pick up where they left off without losing any files.
When Remote Lock is activated, Windows signs out all active sessions, hides local sign-in options, and displays a custom "Device Locked" screen, preventing users from accessing the device locally or remotely. However, locked devices remain enrolled in and managed through Intune, while BitLocker stays enabled as an additional layer of security.
Remote Lock remains enabled across restarts and while the device is offline. Only an administrator can deactivate it. According to Microsoft, the lock can be lifted only remotely through Intune, as there is no way to unlock the device locally. The company says this restriction is intentional and is designed to prevent malicious actors from using brute-force attacks to gain access to device data.

articles.title: “Si hoy fuera el último día de mi vida, ¿querría hacer lo que estoy a punto de hacer?”: Steve Jobs, fundador de Apple

Una de las frases que dejó en 2005 Steve Jobs en su discurso de graduación en la Universidad de Stanford fue una pregunta que convirtió en un método personal para revisar sus decisiones: “Si hoy fuera el último día de mi vida, ¿querría hacer lo que estoy a punto de hacer?”.
El fundador de Apple explicó que la repetición de esa respuesta negativa durante varios días era una señal de que debía modificar algo. El discurso, pronunciado ante graduados, incluyó tres relatos personales sobre los “puntos” que se unen con el tiempo, el amor y la pérdida, y la muerte.
En esta última parte, Jobs vinculó una experiencia médica con una idea que atravesó su vida: la conciencia de que el tiempo es limitado puede ayudar a distinguir entre las expectativas ajenas y las decisiones propias.
Por qué Steve Jobs se hacía la misma pregunta cada día
Jobs contó que, cuando tenía 17 años, leyó una cita que lo marcó: “Si vives cada día como si fuera el último, es muy probable que algún día hagas lo correcto”. A partir de entonces, dijo, integró una rutina frente al espejo.
Durante 33 años, se preguntó cada mañana si elegiría hacer lo que tenía por delante si ese fuera el último día de su vida. La respuesta no era una fórmula para tomar decisiones inmediatas.

articles.title: Supreme Court keeps injunction against DEI grant defunding in place
articles.summary:
On Monday, the Supreme Court announced it would not hear an appeal of a lower court decision that blocked the government from canceling the grants of a handful of researchers whose funding had been revoked during the Trump administration’s purge of DEI-related work. While the decision applies to only seven researchers in California, the lower court had ruled that the government’s actions violated the First Amendment and so may have broad implications.
The Supreme Court provided no discussion of its rejection, and no justices filed a dissent regarding the decision.
The suit was initially filed by a large group of researchers at the University of California, Berkeley and UC San Francisco, contesting grants originally issued by many federal agencies, from the National Institutes of Health to the Department of Transportation. At issue were grants that had been terminated because the agencies decided they violated a Trump executive order blocking the use of DEI. This occurred despite the fact that the government hadn’t bothered to define DEI, and targeted grants were often identified by little more than a keyword search.
In the wake of a Supreme Court decision that held that most grant termination cases had to be heard by a different court, the case was narrowed considerably to just seven UC researchers and a handful of agencies: The Environmental Protection Agency, the National Science Foundation, and the National Endowment for the Humanities.

“This case challenges Comcast’s false advertising campaign for its residential Internet service, marketed under the Xfinity brand to consumers nationwide,” AT&T’s lawsuit said. “At the center of that campaign is Comcast’s claim that Xfinity Internet and its associated Wi-Fi service are ‘Fiber-Powered.’”
While Comcast has deployed plenty of fiber throughout the US, its cable Internet service makes the final connection to homes with coaxial cable. This results in upload speeds being far slower than download speeds.
In contrast, fiber-to-the-home service can provide symmetrical upload and download speeds. Comcast has deployed fiber-to-the-home in only small portions of its cable territory while advertising its service as fiber-powered in the majority of areas where cable makes the final connection.
AT&T’s lawsuit said that in describing its cable broadband as fiber-powered, Comcast “conveys to reasonable consumers the misleading impression that Xfinity Internet is a fiber-to-the-home service comparable to AT&T Fiber. In fact, the vast majority of Xfinity Internet runs over a hybrid fiber-coaxial (‘HFC’) network, where the critical ‘last mile’ connection to the customer’s home uses copper coaxial cable, not fiber.”

articles.title: iPhone Duo gets face unlock, but don't call it Face ID

Apple is testing new iPhone Duo features that will make it easier to unlock and lock the foldable, addressing some of the concerns raised by early adopters.
iOS 27.3 Beta 2 will allow iPhone Duo users to opt in to a face unlock feature that’ll let the Duo cover display camera scan your face and unlock your device, with a few caveats.
First, this isn’t Face ID and is therefore less secure than a regular iPhone’s face-scanning capabilities. Once you start using face unlock, you’ll need to use Touch ID around every 45 minutes for added security. Also, you won’t be able to use face unlock for payments or to get into your passwords, and will need Touch ID again.
The Duo’s face unlock uses the Secure Enclave in the Apple silicon, which privately processes the data of the user’s face and confirms a match. Apple says that iOS, apps, users and even Apple itself cannot access this face data. You can find this feature in Settings, under Touch ID & Passcode.
This is similar to how the Apple HomeView works, since it also doesn’t use the same technology as Face ID. The HomeView requires you to unlock your smartphone every once in a while for its face unlock to work for security purposes as well.
Also coming to the next developer beta for iOS 27.3 is ‘Close to lock,’ which will let you opt in to lock your device every time you close it. You can find this in Settings, under Display & Brightness.

Intel is being sued by shareholders, who are accusing the chipmaker of misleading them about the impact of the PC sales slump that contributed to a drop of 28.6 percent in the price of Intel’s stock on October 30.
The lawsuit (PDF), filed on Friday in the San Jose, California, federal court, is seeking class-action certification and lists the City of Southfield Fire and Police Retirement System and “all others similarly situated” as plaintiffs. In addition to Intel, Intel CEO Lip-Bu Tan and Intel’s EVP and CFO David Zinsner are listed as defendants.
The plaintiffs claim that Intel made “materially false and misleading statements and omissions” between July 23 and October 29. They are seeking unspecified compensatory damages, plus legal and other associated fees, for shareholders during that period.
In the complaint, the shareholders argue that Intel misled them by failing to disclose: the full impact that the PC market sales slump would have on Intel’s third quarter and beyond; the impact of increasing PC component prices on PC sales for Intel’s OEM and distribution partners; that Intel was dealing with substrate supply constraints that would limit its ability to meet data center CPU demand; and “that any positive impacts to Intel’s business and financial results resulting from data center construction and other aspects of the AI boom were more than offset” by the PC sales slump.

Plusieurs médias ont déjà remonté le fil de cette infox, qui ne repose sur rien de concret.
Un simple test d’alerte américain
La date vient pourtant d’un exercice bien réel qui aura lieu de l’autre côté de l’Atlantique. One flashpoint for the tech industry’s all-in push on large language models has been the sudden rush to turn investment money into hyperscale data centers. The rush hasn’t allowed anyone to plan how to supply the required electricity cleanly or with minimal impact on ratepayers. Instead, it has been difficult to even collect information on what’s being built.
A new study has tallied energy use and estimated emissions for hyperscalers operating in the United States between May 2024 and April 2025. They weren’t able to differentiate between AI compute and more traditional data services, but it provides a clear point of reference to track moving forward.
Finding the centers
The team started with a list of 675 facilities from a commercial database based on news reports, company statements, and satellite imagery. They dropped any that didn’t have a reported electrical capacity or that they couldn’t verify was a suitably large building with the expected cooling and electrical connection equipment. That reduced the list to 403 data centers with an average electrical capacity of about 40 megawatts.

The company said it subsequently began notifying affected drivers that their personal information was stored with the provider.
The stolen data includes affected drivers’ names, addresses, dates of birth, and driver’s license numbers.
TechCrunch has learned that the provider is Fireworks AI, which lets developers access and use open-weight AI models. Fireworks reported a data breach last month in which hackers stole its customers’ information, including billing data and some private AI datasets.
Online productivity startup Notion and AI coding startup Cursor have both confirmed that they had data stolen during the Fireworks hack.

India’s deeptech funding hit $914 million in 2025, but limited growth capital, manufacturing dependencies and weak commercialisation pathways continue to hinder startups from scaling.
India’s deeptech companies raised $914 million in 257 rounds in 2025, 34 times the 2016 level. The harder test is turning research and prototypes into commercial products, notes Speciale Invest’s report, India’s Deep Tech Revolution - From the Lab to Growth and Exits.
Using Tracxn data through August 31 2026, the study covers 8,293 private companies worldwide, including 482 in India. India accounted for 12.8% of deeptech funding rounds in 2025 but received 1.6% of the capital.
For every 100 seed rounds, India had 23 Series A or B rounds, against 105 globally. Separately, there was one late-stage or private-equity round per 100 Indian seed rounds, against 26 worldwide. Both measures point to funding thinning as companies mature.
Sectoral advantages are uneven. Space firms can tap ISRO testing facilities and suppliers, while life-sciences ventures can draw on India’s pharmaceutical manufacturing base. Private participation in space has widened since 2020 reforms. Registered space startups rose from one in 2014 to about 440 by August 2026.

The AI reportedly identified the code responsible for enabling the overclocking workaround and modified it to create a BIOS ready for implementation on a compatible motherboard. Non-K models have locked multipliers, which restrict users from pushing CPU frequencies. However, there’s another way to raise the speed of a processor by pushing the base clock itself. In its official report on the incident, OpenAI called it “an outlier scenario involving a rare and unexpected confluence of events.”
The California lawsuit represents one of the first attempts by a government regulator to hold an AI lab legally accountable for a rogue agent incident, with significant implications for both OpenAI’s competitors and its clients.

articles.title: Microsoft outage explained: a three-month-old bug's global impact

Microsoft has finally explained what caused last week’s massive outage, which disrupted businesses and governments worldwide.
The Microsoft 365 outage, which started on Nov. 12 and continued until the morning of Nov. 14, was caused by a combination of issues, including a defect introduced in a July 2026 patch.
Charles Lamanna, Microsoft’s executive vice president of Copilot, Agents, and Platform, took to Twitter/X to share the details behind the outage. First, Lamanna noted that “a latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions.” Notably, Lamanna said the defect was the “result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers” and didn’t impact broader Windows deployments.
The defect was introduced in July, but did not cause any issues until now. Moreover, Lamanna said the defect wasn’t detected by Microsoft’s internal tests, which focused on “weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.” The defect, however, was “worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware.”
The second issue Lamanna highlighted was a surge in load caused by a Teams issue that happened roughly 15 hours before the Microsoft 365 outage. articles.title: New WinPOPBit tool bypasses Windows 11 CPU restrictions to support truly ancient PCs
articles.summary:
In brief: Unlike previous releases, Windows 11 significantly limits the number of systems on which users can attempt to install the new operating system. Needless to say, some developers have recognized Microsoft's challenge and raised the stakes considerably.
A new open-source utility is bringing the latest Windows editions to places where Microsoft developers dared not go. Initially released a few weeks ago, WinPOPBit is designed to "pop" some of the most restrictive hardware requirements in newer Windows 11 versions. The project is progressing rapidly, which means even more ancient CPUs could soon become "compatible" with the latest PC operating systems.
WinPOPBit primarily targets Windows 11's requirement for CPUs with POPCNT and SSE4.2 instruction support, as well as Windows 10's NX bit requirement. Microsoft introduced the new CPU requirements with the Windows 11 24H2 update, preventing OS enthusiasts from installing the latest release on PCs still running decades-old processors.
Despite acknowledging these new "hard" CPU requirements, WinPOPBit's developers have found a way to restore compatibility. The Python tool is essentially an "experimental patcher" capable of modifying a few relevant bytes in Windows system files, allowing newer OS releases to boot and run on CPUs that date back to before Windows 7 was even a thing.

Anthropic told IPO investors that its Claude Mythos Preview model did the software work required to get its AI running on AMD’s GPUs in about three days, with “basically no human intervention,” a job it says used to take six to 12 months. Tom Brown, Anthropic’s co-founder and chief compute officer, made the time comparison, noting to investors that the original meant using a team of “dozens of engineers.” The company already runs its models on multiple kinds of chips — on GPUs from Nvidia and AMD, Google’s TPUs, and AWS Trainium — and its fleet is managed as “one fungible pool of compute.” Brown called the early multi-chip decision “an unconventional bet.” It may have been a wise one, given that Google’s TPUs can now natively run AI models built in PyTorch, and Meta uses them in production.

Building creator trust in the age of AI
There’s always been a balancing act between creators and creator platforms over profit, value, and ownership. Now, AI tools are upsetting that balance and reshaping commercial dynamics, while raising new concerns about transparency and control.
As creators compete for engagement against low-effort AI “slop,” they must also navigate opaque monetization policies and inconsistent enforcement. These pressures are rapidly increasing the friction between creators and the platforms they rely on.
At the same time, as more platforms and revenue streams emerge, creators have greater choice about where to build an audience.

articles.title: Windows 11 sur un iPhone Duo ? Il l'a fait avec Gemini 4 Carbon, et sans jailbreak
articles.summary:
Un responsable de Google a réussi à faire tourner Windows 11 sur le tout premier iPhone pliable d’Apple, avec l’aide de Gemini. Une expérience insolite qui transforme le smartphone en (presque) vrai PC miniature, au prix de quelques acrobaties techniques.
Voilà quelques années, déjà, que Microsoft a jeté l’éponge concernant Windows sur smartphone, mais il semblerait que tout le monde n’ait pas encore renoncé à l’idée. Ammaar Reshi, responsable du produit et du design chez Google AI Studio, vient de publier une vidéo sur X dans laquelle il fait fonctionner Windows 11 sur un iPhone Duo, le tout premier smartphone pliable d’Apple. Pas de jailbreak ni de PC distant pour faire tourner le système, mais un projet développé avec l’aide de Gemini 4 Carbon en seulement deux heures, à en croire son auteur.
Windows 11 et iOS, une cohabitation assez improbable
Baptisé WindowsiOS, le projet ne remplace pas iOS, mais exécute Windows 11 24H2 dans sa version ARM64 au sein d’un environnement virtuel. Pour contourner les restrictions d’Apple sur la virtualisation matérielle, il exploite un moteur de traduction binaire capable d’adapter à la volée les instructions de Windows à l’environnement d’exécution de l’iPhone Duo. Une opération facilitée par l’architecture ARM64 commune au système de Microsoft et à la puce A20 Pro du smartphone.

Detectify’s Agentic Tooling lets AI agents test suspected flaws in running applications
Swedish application security company Detectify AB today launched Agentic Tooling, a set of tools aimed at letting an organization’s own artificial intelligence agents test whether suspected vulnerabilities can be exploited in running applications.
A new Security Ledger, also part of the launch, is designed to record the evidence behind each test. Detectify is pitching the release at DevSecOps teams that are unsure whether they can trust what their AI agents report.
Detectify customers report that roughly 80% of the findings from their AI-driven static application security testing tools are noise. Under pressure to deliver an answer, an agent can also produce a convincing report about a test it never ran, the company warned.
Even before AI agents enter the picture, many security teams are falling behind. Nine in 10 open critical and high-severity vulnerabilities had stayed exposed for more than 90 days, according to Detectify’s H2 2026 Cyber Hygiene Index. In a study by researchers at Fudan University and Tencent Holdings Ltd., 76% of the static-analysis alerts examined were found to be false positives. Each one took developers 10 to 20 minutes to review.

La decisión no establece que hubo un acuerdo ilegal: solo permite que el caso siga.
Los demandantes son 17 consumidores y pequeñas empresas de cinco estados, según la orden judicial. Medios surcoreanos como Seoul Economic Daily precisan que son 14 consumidores y tres ensambladoras y distribuidoras de computadoras, y que presentaron la demanda en junio.
Sostienen que los tres fabricantes recortaron la producción al mismo tiempo, coordinaron el giro hacia la memoria de alto ancho de banda (HBM, el tipo que necesitan los chips de inteligencia artificial) y abandonaron los formatos DDR3 y DDR4. Según la demanda, la oferta de memoria convencional quedó bloqueada mientras los precios subían casi 700%.
La orden recoge otro dato de la demanda: al tercer trimestre de 2025, las tres empresas concentraban más del 91% de los ingresos mundiales de DRAM. SK Hynix tenía el 33,2%, Samsung el 32,6% y Micron el 25,7%. En su pedido de rechazo, las propias compañías admitieron que el sector es un oligopolio, dominado por pocos actores.

articles.title: Microsoft Explains Last Week's 365 Outage
articles.summary:
Monday, November 16th 2026
Microsoft Explains Last Week's 365 Outage
Microsoft has now explained the recent Microsoft 365 outage in a preliminary post-incident report. According to Microsoft, customers were impacted for just under 24 hours, from 4:20 PM UTC on November 12 to 4:10 PM UTC on November 13. The outage prevented many users from accessing their mailboxes in Outlook and delayed email delivery. Moreover, Microsoft Teams, Copilot, SharePoint, and OneDrive were all affected in some way, which is expected since these services all have features that rely on Exchange Online.
The company has traced the outage to three problems that hit Microsoft at the same time. The main culprit is said to be a fix that had been prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 gateway servers. This particular fix, which introduced lock contention in an internal Windows process that exhausted CPU and memory under certain loads, went unnoticed for over three months. That was probably because Microsoft's load testing used weaker machines that couldn't stress the fix properly. Teams also failed over onto the primary gateway it shares with Exchange Online, which worsened the problem. Traffic then shifted to remaining servers, which buckled under the extra load. Apparently, more than 80% of the servers were unresponsive at the worst point of the outage.After that, the recovery process was full of hurdles too. The restored servers were swamped by queued traffic, and the old fix couldn't be hastily undone …

articles.title: Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop - SiliconANGLE
articles.summary:
Google says an AI framework turned security patches into exploits with no human in the loop
A new report out today from Google LLC’s Google Threat Intelligence Group finds that for the first time, attackers have used an artificial intelligence framework running with no human in the loop to turn security patches into exploits.
Called exploit_agent, the framework turned up on an exposed staging server, where it was wired into several frontier and locally hosted large language models. Its job, according to GTIG, is continuous comparison of popular web application code before and after each patch announcement. Once a likely flaw is identified, the exploit it drafts is executed automatically.
Data taken from victims was sitting on the same server, alongside scripts for brute-forcing, installing webshells and even removing webshells left by rival attackers. Victim telemetry suggests the operator was most interested in French websites tied to media, entertainment and education. Written in Russian, one comment in the framework’s configuration file tells whoever set it up to enter the keys “right here, not in the chat.”
In the previous edition of the quarterly tracker two months ago, GTIG said it had not observed fully autonomous attack pipelines deployed against targets in the wild. That changed over the past quarter, according to the new report, titled “Agentic Threat Activity Crosses a Significant Threshold.” Because the source material for a patched flaw is finite, GTIG believes a…

The claim also points to August 2026, when Intel sold $23 billion worth of stock to raise capital, at $95 per share.

articles.title: TRIUMF: Taking a Tour of Canada’s Particle Accelerator - EE Times
articles.summary:
Canada’s particle accelerator is smaller than CERN’s flagship Large Hadron Collider, but it occupies a distinct place in the international research ecosystem: TRIUMF combines high-intensity beams, rare-isotope production, and specialized materials probes, including capabilities that advance semiconductor research.
Located on the University of British Columbia’s (UBC’s) main, forested campus in Vancouver, the research center was conceived in 1965 as the Tri-University Meson Facility, a joint initiative of UBC, Simon Fraser University, and the University of Victoria. The addition of the University of Alberta as a founding partner soon made the original name less apt. Cyclotron construction began in 1971 and was officially commissioned in 1974. Now the facility is simply known as TRIUMF and is run by a consortium of 21 member universities across Canada.
TRIUMF’s strengths lie in rare‑isotope beams, beta-detected nuclear magnetic resonance (β‑NMR), muon spin rotation (μSR), and dedicated nuclear‑astrophysics spectrometers. TRIUMF often contributes specialized detector components, accelerator technology, and computing expertise to large, international experiments, including those at CERN, while its facilities serve as Canada’s main hub for accelerator‑based science and isotope supply.
At the heart of the 13.5-acre site is the 520-MeV cyclotron, the world’s largest normal-conducting cyclotron. The machine is 18 meters across, its pinwheel-shaped magnet weighs 4,000 metric tons, and…

Copycats are still slipping past Chrome's defenses
Last month, TechRadar published an investigation highlighting 369 suspicious VPN extensions targeting Russian users. Since then, Google has removed all but seven of them.
Many of the purged extensions used throwaway, personal developer emails, had inadequate privacy policies and mimicked well-known brands, including ExpressVPN and Windscribe. Several had even been flagged in threat intelligence reports months before.
While the removal of these apps is a positive step, a quick look through the Web Store shows that there’s still work to be done.
Hundreds of shady VPN extensions removed
Our initial investigation flagged more than 350 extensions targeting Russian civilians, which had over 200,000 users combined.
VPNs have become a critical tool in Russia owing to heightened internet censorship and surveillance. Unfortunately, this also means they have become a prime target for groups looking to turn a quick profit.
We shared details of all the extensions included in our investigation with Google ahead of publication and, less than one month later, almost all of them have been removed from the Chrome Web Store.
Google did not respond to requests for comment to confirm whether the extensions were removed as a result of our investigation or as part of routine maintenance of the store.

articles.summary:
New US rules aim to close loophole, restrict Chinese firms’ remote access to AI servers and infrastructure — seeks to combat cloud rental workarounds to export controls
The Bureau of Industry and Security has released an interim final rule to ensure physical restrictions cannot be bypassed by using cloud-based infrastructure.
New steps have been taken to ensure that countries and companies that are not on whitelists that would allow them to import advanced AI hardware cannot use cloud-based workarounds. articles.summary:
Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max with training, attention optimizations
Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. today introduced Qwen4-Max, its newest and most capable large language model.
The algorithm not only generates higher-quality output than its predecessor but also costs less. Those improvements are the result of a new architecture, Qwen4, that made the LLM’s training run more efficient. Additionally, Alibaba has equipped the model with an upgraded attention mechanism.
Qwen4-Max’s backbone, the part of an LLM that functions as its main processing engine, comprises 2.4 trillion parameters. The model activates only 71 billion at any given time. The backbone is supported by 328 billion so-called N-gram parameters, which function as a kind of cache. They save the results of oft-repeated calculations and thereby remove the need to compute them from scratch every time.
An LLM’s artificial neurons are organized into sets known as layers. When the model learns something new during training, a piece of data called a gradient travels through the layers and refines their output. The gradient moves through them one by one starting from the last layer, which finalizes and displays prompt responses.
Qwen4-Max includes a feature that enables the gradient to skip some layers. That feature, or residual, is effectively a shortcut inside the LLM. Its purpose is to reduce errors during the training workflow, which in turn lowers costs and improves output quality.

articles.title: KDE Plasma 6.9 Cuts Overhead with On-Demand XWayland Implementation
articles.summary:
Monday, November 16th 2026
KDE Plasma 6.9 Cuts Overhead with On-Demand XWayland Implementation
KDE Plasma is one of the most commonly recommended Linux desktop environments, thanks to its flexibility, frequent updates, and surprisingly low performance footprint. According to the latest issue of This Week in Plasma by KDE's Nate Graham, KDE Plasma 6.9 will introduce a more streamlined implementation of XWayland. 
The big change would enable XWayland—the compatibility layer that enables compatibility with legacy X11 apps—to run on-demand. That is to say that XWayland will only run when the user or system launch an application that requires the compatibility layer, as opposed to running in the background all the time.Other notable mentions include speed improvements for both the KDE screenshot utility, Spectacle, and for the Add Widgets sidebar on the desktop. The KDE Login Manager also now includes an automatic terminal fallback when it fails. Several customization and settings pages have also received small tweaks that make them more intuitive to use more visually appealing. The network widget also now includes an option to forget networks, instead of making users open the setting app to do it, and the System Monitor app and widgets also include a sensor to list physical CPU cores.
Sources:
				This Week in Plasma, 				via Phoronix

articles.title: Cómo evitar que mi vecino esté conectado a mi red WiFi y mejorar la velocidad del internet
articles.summary:
Una conexión lenta, cortes frecuentes o dispositivos desconocidos en la lista del router pueden indicar que alguien ajeno al hogar como un vecino usa la red WiFi.
En este sentido, se explican varios ajustes que se pueden realizar en casa para proteger la red de internet de intrusos que no solo roben banda de ancha; pueden en casos más graves intentar acceder a datos guardados en los dispositivos conectados.
Qué ajustes hacer en la configuración inicial del router
El router funciona como la puerta de entrada a internet de teléfonos, ordenadores, televisores, cámaras y otros dispositivos conectados. Si mantiene sus parámetros iniciales, una persona con conocimientos básicos puede identificar el modelo, buscar sus claves predeterminadas e intentar entrar al panel de control.
Las credenciales de fábrica de muchos routers están disponibles en manuales, foros y sitios web. Cambiar el usuario y la contraseña de administración permite recuperar el control sobre la red y evita que una clave conocida por terceros abra la puerta a la configuración interna del dispositivo.
El primer paso consiste en conectar un ordenador al router mediante un cable de red. Esa vía permite realizar los cambios desde una conexión directa, sin depender del WiFi que se busca proteger. Antes de modificar opciones, conviene anotar los datos actuales o tomar capturas de pantalla de la configuración.

Las empresas designadas recibirían aprobaciones aceleradas de licencias de exportación de chips y otras tecnologías, apoyo del gobierno para sus operaciones en el extranjero y acceso a financiamiento federal, según el informe.
La idea es agrupar chips, modelos de IA y otras tecnologías en paquetes que gobiernos y empresas de otros países puedan comprar, en lugar de negociar con cada compañía por separado. Cada venta individual seguiría necesitando una autorización.

articles.summary:
Investigadores de MinoHealth AI Labs, un laboratorio de inteligencia artificial de Accra, Ghana, quitaron las barreras de seguridad de su modelo para descubrir medicamentos y le pidieron diseñar toxinas. El programa generó diseños de 1.020 proteínas y 5.000 moléculas pequeñas que un software de predicción calificó como probablemente tóxicas.
Los investigadores no fabricaron ninguna de esas sustancias en un laboratorio. Algunos diseños se parecían a la ricina, un veneno mortal. El estudio se subió en mayo de 2025 al servidor de preprints arXiv, según informó Rest of World.
“Todos quedamos impactados”, dijo a ese medio Darlington Akogo, fundador de MinoHealth. El experimento se hizo en 2024 y, según Akogo, bastaron unos pocos días para que el modelo, llamado Moremi Bio, ignorara sus salvaguardas.
Akogo sostiene que su trabajo fue el primero en mostrar que un modelo de lenguaje puede diseñar armas biológicas. Antes, en 2022, científicos de una farmacéutica de Estados Unidos habían usado un programa de aprendizaje automático para generar diseños de posibles armas químicas.
El eslabón pendiente: la fabricación de ADN
La preocupación de Akogo va más allá del diseño. Alguien podría enviar esas secuencias a una empresa que fabrica ADN por encargo. Algunas de estas compañías revisan los pedidos para detectar secuencias tóxicas, pero un actor malicioso podría burlar ese filtro con ayuda de la IA, advirtió.

articles.title: Amazon Uncovers AI Agent Campaign Targeting LiteLLM, Dify, and Other Apps for API Keys
articles.summary:
Attackers' AI agents have been hunting for weak spots in internet-exposed AI apps such as LiteLLM, One API, and Dify to steal the AI provider keys stored inside, according to the agents' own records.
The records, which Amazon's threat intelligence team captured with decoy servers, describe stolen keys being used to run the AI models that powered the search for more keys.
The team said this week that it cannot verify the outcomes reported by the agents. It has moderate confidence that the agents ran on ARTEX, an open-source AI tool for penetration testing.
The records include a playbook of known entry points for each targeted product. It lists default administrator credentials such as LiteLLM's default master key, unfinished installs that an outsider could take over, and known flaws in Langflow and RAGFlow.
In a separate case reported this week, Cloudflare's incident responders saw ARTEX gain access to a compromised API token that had been used for CI/CD. The token had no IP restrictions or rate limiting, and the activity that followed included 400 database dump requests in an hour. The company has not said whether those requests returned any data.
An operator gives ARTEX a target and a goal, and a planner agent splits the goal into tasks for worker agents that run security tools. To decide each next step, the agents send their work to a large language model (LLM).

Central to the intrusion is a toolkit called SANSAR, a Rust-based orchestrator that receives commands over the TOR anonymity network to manage CPU and GPU miners. The activity was observed in late October 2026.
"The threat actor also deployed a kernel rootkit to hide selected processes and files, an NVIDIA Management Library (NVML) wrapper to falsify GPU readings, and a separate backdoor named netns," Elastic Security Labs said in a report published last week.
"This backdoor retrieves its C2 [command-and-control] address from an Ethereum smart contract before connecting to the server directly."
In the attack chain documented by the company, initial access is said to have been achieved via an exposed Ray job agent, allowing the threat actor to execute commands. This includes jobs running the NVIDIA System Management Interface (nvidia-smi) to capture and exfiltrate the GPU inventory to an external server.
Subsequently, the attacker submitted a Python reverse shell job that connected to a remote listener, after which an SSH key was added to that account's authorized_keys file to establish persistent access.

Government cybersecurity agencies in Belgium, Ireland and Germany told operators this week to take the controllers' management interfaces off the internet.
For a controller left on the internet, updating the firmware, changing default passwords or turning on Strict mode is not enough on its own, the Belgian and Irish agencies said. Strict mode is a login protection that requires encrypted connections and session tokens, but one of the six flaws is in the gateway that enforces it.
The AK-SM800A runs a store's fridges and freezers, and maintenance firms can manage it remotely. Such controllers were targeted in attacks in France starting October 11, and in a second wave across Europe that began last week. The attacks caused unwanted defrost cycles and destroyed stock.
Germany's federal IT security agency, the BSI, says in a security notice that the AK-SM800A was involved in earlier incidents in which refrigeration units in several countries were tampered with.
The agency has no information about any exploitation of the six new flaws, and neither other agencies nor researchers link the flaws to those incidents.

articles.title: Crean un sensor portátil que podría detectar químicos eternos en el agua: cómo funciona
articles.summary:
El agua puede parecer limpia y contener rastros de sustancias conocidas como químicos eternos, que persisten durante décadas. Para identificarlas sin depender siempre de un laboratorio, el Instituto de Ciencia y Tecnología de Okinawa (Japón) creó un sensor portátil capaz de detectar PFAS en agua.
El desafío es llevar el análisis al lugar donde se toma la muestra. Los métodos habituales son precisos, pero requieren equipos especializados, trasladar las muestras y contar con instrumentos costosos. El prototipo propone una primera medición con una tira flexible conectada a un aparato de lectura.
El dispositivo se ensayó con PFOA y PFOS, dos compuestos de la familia de las PFAS, en agua potable y dulce. El avance se describe en un estudio publicado en la revista Biosensors and Bioelectronics. Vale destacar que se trata de resultados iniciales y aún necesitan validación en otras condiciones ambientales.
Las PFAS persisten y por eso resulta difícil vigilar su presencia
Las sustancias perfluoroalquiladas y polifluoroalquiladas, conocidas como PFAS, se usan en materiales resistentes al agua, el aceite y el calor. Esa resistencia también dificulta que se degraden, por lo que pueden acumularse en el agua, el suelo y los organismos, según el comunicado del instituto.
El estudio abordó la detección de dos de esos compuestos en concentraciones muy bajas con una herramienta que pueda trasladarse. Para ello, el equipo fabricó nanopartículas de polímeros de impresión molecular, un material d…

AMD is adding tamper-resistant hardware to its chips to protect from physical attacks
AMD is building backside protection into the silicon
- AMD's Versal TR adaptive SoCs bond a sensor die to the silicon backside that detects physical attacks and blocks boot if removed
- Post-quantum ML-DSA and SLH-DSA acceleration arrives after rivals Altera and Lattice already shipped post-quantum secure boot
- Samples are not due until the second half of 2027, and AMD itself says tamper-resistant does not mean tamper-proof
AMD has unveiled a family of adaptive chips with their own built-in bodyguard.
The company's new Versal tamper-resistant devices bond a sensor-based protection die to the back of the main compute die, where it shields the silicon, watches for physical attacks, and stops the chip from booting if it is tampered with or removed.
The chips, specifically the 2VE3358TR, 2VE3558TR and 2VE3858TR, are all variants of the Versal AI Edge Series Gen 2 adaptive SoCs that AMD first unveiled alongside Arm in 2024, and will look to cater to the likes of defense systems, data center networking, financial technology and critical industrial infrastructure.
A second die guarding the side that nobody watches?
One might ponder why the backside is suddenly important: most high-performance chips are flip-chip packaged, mounted face down, so the transistors sit against the package while the bare silicon substrate faces up.

Un enlace de afiliado es una dirección web que identifica al creador que recomendó un producto, de modo que Amazon le pague un porcentaje cuando alguien compra. Hasta ahora, los creadores compartían esos vínculos en historias, mensajes privados o en la biografía de su perfil.
La función llega por ahora solo a Estados Unidos. Según Wired, los creadores deben ser adultos residentes en ese país, con una cuenta profesional y más de 1.000 seguidores. Engadget informó que Meta, la dueña de Instagram, no dijo si la extenderá a otros países.
Para activarla, el creador conecta su cuenta de Instagram con su cuenta de influenciador de Amazon desde la sección de monetización del panel profesional, según TechCrunch. Después, la red social agrega sola el enlace de afiliado cuando se etiqueta un producto de Amazon, aunque el creador pegue un enlace común.
Quién cobra y cómo se ve el enlace
Instagram afirmó que agregar los productos es gratis y que no cobra comisión ni cargos por transacción. Amazon sigue pagando las comisiones, y el creador puede ver la tasa estimada de cada producto antes de sumarlo a su contenido.

articles.title: Samsung fabriquerait au Texas des puces pour Starlink

Le microcontrôleur que SpaceX a installé dans le système laser de ses satellites Starlink est fabriqué par STMicroelectronics à Crolles, près de Grenoble. Selon le Seoul Economic Daily, Samsung produirait une partie de ces puces dans son usine d’Austin, au Texas, d’ici 2030, près du site où SpaceX assemble ses kits Starlink.
Dans un microcontrôleur, le fabricant réunit sur une seule petite puce un processeur et de la mémoire, pour piloter une tâche précise. STMicroelectronics grave son STM32V8 en 18 nanomètres sur FD-SOI. Avec cette technique, la couche de silicium des transistors est posée sur un fin isolant, et les puces sont moins sensibles aux radiations de l’espace. Samsung a mis au point ce procédé avec le groupe franco-italien, et d’après le quotidien économique sud-coréen, il investirait 1,9 milliard de dollars pour agrandir son usine d’Austin et graver au Texas une partie des STM32V8 qui sortent aujourd’hui de l’usine de Crolles.
Samsung agrandit son usine d’Austin pour l’aérospatiale et la défense
Samsung produit des puces à Austin depuis 1996, avec des finesses de gravure de 65 à 14 nanomètres, loin des 2 nanomètres de sa nouvelle usine de Taylor, à une cinquantaine de kilomètres. Pour ses deux sites texans, le Département américain du Commerce lui a accordé jusqu’à 4,745 milliards de dollars de subventions publiques.
